articles.body: Donna Kelce has stepped forward to defend her son, Kansas City Chiefs star Travis Kelce, as old social media posts attributed to the NFL tight end draw renewed attention. The controversy has raised questions about the authenticity of the messages and added fresh scrutiny to the athlete's online activity. Donna rejected claims that the posts belonged to Travis, pushing back against allegations that have spread across social media. Her response comes amid separate criticism surrounding Travis's reported interaction with a controversial comedy clip, placing the football star at the centre of another online debate.Donna Kelce challenges claims about Travis Kelce's old tweetsDonna, 74, addressed the issue on X on Saturday, October 17, after a fan shared screenshots of messages allegedly posted between 2009 and 2011. The posts, linked to an account named “tkelce”, reportedly included offensive comments about women's appearances, cheerleaders and other people.One screenshot shows a tweet reading, “hahaha why cant girls hide they backfat? that ***** nasty!!!” Another reads, “I feel like if u wanna be a cheerleader you have to pass a beauty test…. there’s too many ugly cheerleaders out here smh.”Her response was direct. “Not Travis’ handle and not his account!!” she wrote, disputing the connection between her son and the messages.The statement puts the focus on a key question in the controversy: whether the account and its historical posts can be reliably linked to Travis. The messages date back more than a decade, long before his current status as one of the NFL's most recognisable players.However, the claims have a documented history. The New York Times reported in 2023 that fact-checking website Snopes had independently verified the tweets. That earlier reporting adds context to the renewed debate, although Donna's latest statement challenges the account's association with her son.Travis, 37, has not publicly addressed the resurfaced posts. His silence leaves questions unanswered as fans continue to discuss the allegations and Donna's defence.Fans clash over Donna Kelce's defence of her sonHowever, several users pushed back against her statement. And why are you battling for him? Does he need his mom to stick up for him at 37?“Or, is this a threat to the Marriage National Bank of Taylor Swift?”Another user, Liza, also challenged Donna's denial, writing, “but Donna that screenshot was absolutely from Travis’s twitter, sorry to say. The tweets have been deleted now but he did tweet that about ugly cheerleaders, sorry 🤷‍♀️”The reaction was not entirely negative towards Donna. Some fans urged people to consider Travis's age when the alleged messages appeared.One user, SugarSkull3192, defended the NFL star, writing, “You people are insane. Leave his mother alone. articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes are facing fresh scrutiny over the Kansas City Current’s plans to expand its home stadium, CPKC Stadium, despite the
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes are facing fresh scrutiny over the Kansas City Current’s plans to expand its home stadium, CPKC Stadium, despite the venue opening only in March 2024. The ownership group reportedly wants to increase capacity from 11,500 to 18,000 seats, with a proposed public financing package worth $185 million drawing attention. The debate centres on a familiar question in professional sports: should taxpayers help fund projects connected to wealthy team owners? While the expansion could create opportunities for more events, the proposed funding arrangement has raised concerns about how public money would support a privately owned sports development.Patrick and Brittany Mahomes face questions over KC Current stadium expansionThe Kansas City Current made history with CPKC Stadium, the first purpose-built stadium for a National Women's Soccer League team. The venue opened on March 16, 2024, after the ownership group invested $117 million in construction.Patrick and Brittany Mahomes are among the club's high-profile owners, alongside business partners who helped establish the team's wider development ambitions. The stadium also received $5.5 million from Missouri's Development Finance Board for infrastructure, according to Sports Talk NY Fan.Now, the ownership group's proposed expansion has renewed questions about the cost of upgrading such a new venue. Increasing capacity to 18,000 seats could allow the Current to host larger crowds and attract events beyond regular NWSL matches. However, critics may question why a stadium opened just two years ago needs further investment supported by a public financing arrangement.The proposal also forms part of a broader vision for a stadium village, with retail and other developments planned around the venue. The ownership group reportedly wants public support to help move that vision forward.KC Current’s $185 million public funding proposal raises concernsThe proposed $185 million package would use tax incremental financing, a mechanism that redirects certain future tax revenues generated within a development area towards eligible project costs.Under the arrangement described by Sports Talk NY Fan, sales taxes generated by the planned retail development would be directed back to developers rather than flowing entirely into the municipality's general fund. The report also states that the ownership group would issue bonds and assume the associated debt, with redirected economic activity taxes helping repay the costs.The key question is whether the development would generate enough additional economic activity to justify the public contribution. Supporters could argue that a larger stadium and surrounding businesses would attract visitors, create jobs and bring more spending to Kansas City. Critics, meanwhile, may question the public benefit if the retail village does not develop as planned.The proposal is not yet a completed funding deal. Kansas City officials have instructed City Manager Mario Vasquez to negotiate with the team and explore applicable Missouri tax incentives.For Patrick and Brittany Mahomes and their fellow owners, the expansion could strengthen the Current's long-term commercial appeal. But the funding debate highlights the challenge facing cities when private sports ambitions rely on public financial support.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: "My daughter doesn't deserve this": Tom Brady shuts down radio interview after host insults his young daughter Vivian
articles.summary: Tom Brady spent years handling pressure on the football field, but an insult aimed at his young daughter pushed him to take a firm stand off it.
articles.body: Tom Brady spent years handling pressure on the football field, but an insult aimed at his young daughter pushed him to take a firm stand off it. In 2018, the NFL legend ended a radio interview after a host made a harsh remark about five-year-old Vivian. His response drew attention to an issue that goes beyond celebrity families: children should not become targets of public ridicule. Brady’s reaction was direct, personal and a reminder that fame does not make a parent any less protective of their child.Tom Brady ends radio interview after remarks about VivianThe incident took place in 2018, during Brady’s weekly appearance on WEEI’s The Kirk & Callahan Show. The New England Patriots quarterback had maintained a working relationship with the programme for years, regularly joining its hosts to discuss football. However, the atmosphere changed after co-host Alex Reimer made an insulting comment about Vivian while discussing a video featuring her.Reimer reportedly called the young girl an “annoying little pi**ant.” Brady did not treat the remark as harmless banter. Instead, he made it clear that the comment had crossed a personal boundary and cut the interview short.“I’ve tried to come on this show for many years and showed you guys a lot of respect,” Brady said during his weekly segment on WEEI’s The Kirk & Callahan Show. “I’ve always tried and come on and do a good job for you guys. It’s very disappointing when you hear that, certainly. My daughter, or any child, they certainly don’t deserve that.”His response highlighted the difference between criticism of a public figure and an attack on a child. Brady had spent much of his career under intense media scrutiny, but he did not believe his daughter should face the same treatment.Why Tom Brady’s response sent a message about child shamingBrady’s reaction also raised questions about the boundaries of sports commentary. Radio hosts often rely on humour, strong opinions and provocative remarks to attract listeners. Yet a child’s behaviour in a video should not become an excuse for personal insults, especially when the child is too young to understand the wider attention.Following the incident, Brady said he was reconsidering whether he would return to the programme. His decision showed that professional relationships do not have to take priority when a family member is involved.The episode offered a wider lesson for parents, fans and media personalities. Children are still learning how to express themselves, manage emotions and behave in unfamiliar situations. They will make mistakes, act silly and sometimes test boundaries. Those moments are part of growing up, not an invitation for adults to shame them.Brady’s response was a reminder that public figures and their families deserve basic respect. Criticism may come with fame, but children should not have to carry that burden. Protecting them from cruel comments is not about avoiding accountability. articles.summary: Jason and Travis Kelce are giving one lucky couple a wedding that will be anything but ordinary.
articles.body: Jason and Travis Kelce are giving one lucky couple a wedding that will be anything but ordinary. Their beer brand, Garage Beer, plans to bring wedding bells to an Philadelphia Eagles tailgate, blending football, live music and the kind of party that reflects the city’s sporting culture. The October 26 celebration arrives at a crucial time for the company, which recently secured a $20 million financing deal to fuel its expansion. For the Kelce brothers, the unusual event offers more than a memorable day for a couple. It also gives their growing brand another chance to stand out in a crowded beer market.Garage Beer brings a wedding celebration to an Eagles tailgateGarage Beer and True Fan Tailgate will host the event in Philadelphia on October 26, with one selected couple exchanging vows in front of football fans. The celebration will feature former Eagles defensive tackle Beau Allen, along with musical performances by Delco Donny and Philly Pops. Food prepared on Kingsford charcoal grills will add to the tailgate atmosphere.Guests can expect Garage Beer Classic and Garage Beer Lime at the event. The couple will also receive a $2,000 gift card toward wedding rings from Philadelphia jeweller Steven Singer and a honeymoon at Ocean Casino Resort in Atlantic City, New Jersey.The location has a personal connection to Jason Kelce, who spent all 13 seasons of his NFL career with the Eagles. He became one of the franchise’s most recognisable players and helped Philadelphia win Super Bowl LII. His lasting bond with the city makes it a natural setting for a promotion built around football and local pride.Garage Beer has often used humour and sports connections to reach customers. Earlier campaigns included Brotherly Shovel, a Western-themed advertisement featuring Jason and Allen shovelling manure, and Brewmite II, a 17-minute promotional film.Jason explained his approach to advertising in an August 2025 interview with People, saying, “I don’t think we should over-complicate it,” Jason told People in August 2025 while discussing the brand’s advertisements. “When it comes to beer, I think when you’re having fun and you’re being personable, you’re being creative, all the best beer ads I know are fun, creative.”Garage Beer secures $20 million to support expansionThe wedding promotion follows Garage Beer’s October 13 financing agreement with Tiger Finance. The $20 million deal will help the company enter additional markets and develop more products.Based in Columbus, Ohio, Garage Beer has been led by Andy Sauer since 2023. Jason and Travis joined as co-owners and operators in June 2024, bringing their sporting reputations and large fan bases to the business.Durational Capital Management announced a strategic investment partnership with Garage Beer in September 2025. Its co-founder, Patrick Khayat, welcomed the latest financing arrangement.“We appreciate Tiger’s creativity and partnership to structure a credit facility that leverages the strength of Garage Beer’s brand to support the Company’s growth objectives,” Khayat said.Tiger Finance also praised the brothers’ contribution to the brand’s visibility. With fresh financing and creative promotions, Garage Beer is looking to turn celebrity recognition into lasting business growth. articles.title: 'They can trust me': As J.J. McCarthy explodes in fourth quarter of yo-yo Giants-Saints game, John Harbaugh now has decision to make
articles.summary: Giants head coach John Harbaugh declined to name a starter after the game. Nine questions later, his tone had shifted slightly. When would he start the proce...
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — When J.J. McCarthy was thrust onto the field Sunday , he had never thrown a live pass to New York Giants teammate Malik Nabers.

He had never thrown more than a sideline or warm-up ball to tight end Isaiah Likely.

Three weeks ago, McCarthy had never even heard a Giants play-call.

So when he took his first snap under center with 11:25 to play in the fourth quarter, the Giants trailing by 24, thanks in large part to three turnovers, McCarthy seemed more likely to continue the hole-digging than reverse trend.

An interception on his fourth pass furthered that theory.

Then, he rebounded to the tune of 269 yards from scrimmage and three scoring drives — all in the fourth quarter.

"I thought he came in there and did a heck of a job given the circumstances, you know, and kind of desperation time," head coach John Harbaugh said after the Giants' 34-27 loss dropped them to 3-2-1. "It's different than normal football, but [he] made some plays and got us back, gives us a chance to win the game and we're throwing the ball in the end zone at the end so that was good.

McCarthy's play, in his first meaningful quarterback action since the Giants dealt a fifth-round draft pick for him on Sept. 28 (he has spotted for a trick play here and there), firmly thrust him into the conversation of Giants starting quarterback ahead of the Giants' visit next week to a gaining-momentum Houston Texans team .

Harbaugh declined to name a starter on Sunday after the game.

"I can't answer it now," Harbaugh said early in his postgame media conference. "It's not even up for discussion or conversation right now. We've got to go back and go to work. I have no problem with Jameis whatsoever. I love the way he competes, I love the way he fights, all those kind of things. He was up and down today for sure, but those things will all be decided not 10 minutes after a game."

Nine questions later, Harbaugh's tone had shifted slightly. When would he start the process of deciding whether to change quarterbacks?

After 34-10 deficit, McCarthy helped Giants rally back

As the first half neared its end, McCarthy's day seemed likely to reflect his last two Sundays: a keeper or trick play here and there, but otherwise no action.

Winston had beaten the Tennessee Titans and Arizona Cardinals right before and after the Giants acquired McCarthy as depth following Jaxson Dart's season-ending knee surgery. The Giants had tied the Washington Commanders last week thanks in part to botched clock management by Jayden Daniels and co .

As long as Winston wasn't losing games for the Giants, at least some inside the building expected him to keep his job. Then, the Saints hit a field goal with 1:23 to play in the half, Giants kick returner Charlie Jones fumbled on the next play, and Saints quarterback Tyler Shough hit receiver Bryce Lance for a touchdown with five seconds to go. A 10-point lead was suddenly a tie at half. Within three minutes of the second half, Saints running back Alvin Kamara scored another touchdown.

The Saints had scored 27 unanswered points by third quarter's end, aided by a Winston-to-Nabers pass intercepted with 4:23 to play in the third.

Once Winston's next two outings featured a three-and-out and a second interception, his day was done. Harbaugh had already sent a message to the fumbling running back Cam Skattebo, who received no carries vs. the Saints (Harbaugh insisted Skattebo getting zero carries after 12 to 20 in each previous game was "not by design" even as Skattebo acknowledged he was being punished.)

Why not send a message to the interception-throwing Winston, too?

"Just left a lot of plays out there that I could have executed better on," said Winston, who completed 14-of-26 attempts for 152 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions.

After McCarthy's first series ended in an interception, he rebounded to lead consecutive touchdown drives with completions of 27, 49 and 24 yards to Nabers, Jones and Likely.

Color analyst Drew Brees praised how McCarthy layered throws and gave his targets a chance, including an airborne Likely for the touchdown. Another field-goal drive and two defensive stops, and the Giants were driving again in the final minute, with the game on the line.

Likely ultimately didn't catch McCarthy's fourth-and-1 shot to the end zone. But the energy in the locker room seemed to shift with how McCarthy rallied them back.

"It just felt at home in terms of just playing quarterback, just being able to run the whole show and make protection calls and be able to throw the ball a little bit …" McCarthy said from the postgame locker room. "I hope I just showed them that I can do my job at a high enough level that they can trust me out there."

Even without Harbaugh endorsing McCarthy as the starter going forward, a locker room fond of Winston personally had gained respect for McCarthy professionally.

"I think he just showed a spark," fullback Patrick Ricard said from his locker. "And that's no knock on Jameis. I feel like Jameis has been playing his heart out and doing everything he can to help us win. But I feel like when J.J. came in, he just had a let-it-rip mentality of 'I'm just going to throw this thing, throw it up and try to make the guys make plays,' and they all did.

"I think that was the biggest thing is just giving guys chances and opportunities to make the plays, and he made some plays with his feet, which is really encouraging, and I was happy for him."

Harbaugh, too, was willing to praise McCarthy's mobility even as he eschewed several other questions after the loss.

McCarthy used his mobility to elude the sack and climb up the pocket on his 46-yard completion to Nabers. He tucked and ran 28 yards upfield in the final minute to keep the game alive. And he used it to roll out of the pocket on his final dart, though he said afterward he wished he extended that play still longer.

"It's a big asset for him, absolutely," Harbaugh said. "He's a very mobile quarterback. Absolutely, that's a plus for him. Sure. Big part of his skill set."

Will Harbaugh choose to prioritize that skill set over Winston's experience in the coming weeks? The Giants' interest in McCarthy stemmed, in part, from his similarities in skill set (if not the same track record yet) to Dart, whom the Giants designed their offense around.

Ricard, who played nine seasons for Harbaugh in Baltimore before joining him for a 10th in New York, said merit would lead the decision.

"Ever since I've known Harbs, he's always been [for fielding] the best guy to play," Ricard said. "Year 10 with him now, it's still true. If you play well, you'll keep playing. If you don't play well, then he's going to find somebody that will play well and give them those opportunities.

"I think that's just whenever you play, you just have to seize opportunities and just do the best you can with it."

The Giants could opt to give Winston next week's start against the Texans, knowing their bye week and a longer run-up to prepare McCarthy follows afterward.

The Giants remain atop a struggling NFC East, with the Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys falling to 2-4 Sunday while the Washington Commanders enter "Monday Night Football" with one win.

Winston has completed 90-of-158 attempts (57%) for 957 yards, 7 touchdowns and 5 interceptions while leading the Giants to 2-1-1. McCarthy completed 11-of-21 (52.4%) for 243 yards, 1 touchdown and 1 interception, his 90.0 passer rating more efficient than Winston's 76.4.

What would McCarthy look like after a week of game-planning around his skill set and giving him practice reps with the starters?

He declined to publicly advocate for himself.

"The only thing I'm focused on is getting better each and every day," McCarthy said. "At the end of the day, Coach Harbaugh has to make a lot of decisions, and those are his decisions. And I trust him wholeheartedly with anything he makes, any decision he makes.

"And at the end of the day, I'm just focused on getting better from this."

articles.title: NFL results: Los Angeles Rams lose again as Kansas City Chiefs stay unbeaten
articles.summary: Week six in the NFL produced some unlikely heroes as the Arizona Cardinals pulled off a huge upset while the Philadelphia Eagles suffered another loss.
articles.body:
Week six in the NFL produced some unlikely heroes as the Arizona Cardinals pulled off the biggest upset of the season so far.

Kicker Chad Ryland scored all of Arizona's points at the Los Angeles Rams to leave the former Super Bowl favourites bottom of the NFC West division.

The Philadelphia Eagles continued to struggle but their former Super Bowl rivals the Kansas City Chiefs remained unbeaten.

The Cleveland Browns maintained their surprise start while the Houston Texans concluded this year's London series by winning a thriller at Wembley.

Here are five things you need to know from Sunday's action.

The Los Angeles Rams started the season as the clearest Super Bowl favourites in nine years but were replaced by the San Francisco 49ers after last Monday's overtime defeat by the Buffalo Bills.

They cut kicker Harrison Mevis on Tuesday and signed Blake Grupe from the New York Jets' practice squad, and although Grupe's field goal opened the scoring against Arizona, he injured a knee while making a tackle from the ensuing kick-off.

The Rams edged back in front with 47 seconds remaining as punter Ethan Evans took on the kicking duties to add the extra point after Colby Parkinson's touchdown.

But Arizona hit straight back and a career-high sixth field goal by Chad Ryland clinched an 18-16 win as time expired.

After just three wins last season, the Cardinals now have two this year and both have come at SoFi Stadium having also beaten the Los Angeles Chargers in week one.

Arizona also crept above the Rams in a division which features the unbeaten 49ers and defending champions the Seattle Seahawks.

"We've got to be able to figure it out and it starts with me," said the Rams' head coach Sean McVay.

Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes reached 100 regular-season wins in his 131st start, tying Tom Brady's record.

After missing out on last season's play-offs, the Chiefs boosted their roster by signing the Super Bowl's Most Valuable Player Kenneth Walker and he rushed for another 128 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 22-6 win over the Chargers.

The running back now leads the NFL with 665 rushing yards, a record from a player's first five games with a new team, and the Chiefs visit his former team Seattle next Sunday.

Kansas City and the Minnesota Vikings are now 5-0 while San Francisco - the only other unbeaten team after five wins - are at home to Washington on Monday night.

The Buffalo Bills held on for a 33-30 win at the Las Vegas Raiders to improve to 5-1 while Caleb Williams returned from a hamstring injury to help the Chicago Bears to a 31-23 win at the Atlanta Falcons.

The Philadelphia Eagles were already struggling with injuries before last Sunday's loss to Jacksonville at Tottenham.

They then revealed that quarterback Jalen Hurts played that game with a superficial blood clot in his calf and a follow-up ultrasound showed that it had moved.

The 2025 Super Bowl winner was then placed on injured reserve so will miss at least four weeks, with back-up Tanner McKee coming in for his third NFL start at home to the Carolina Panthers.

Tight end Tommy Tremble scored his first two touchdowns of the season as the Panthers won 25-14, meaning the Eagles have lost four straight games for the first time since Nick Sirianni became head coach in 2021.

Offensive linemen Lane Johnson (retirement) and Cam Jurgens (traded to Baltimore) both left the team two weeks ago and after seeing the Eagles reach two of the past four Super Bowls, many Philly fans fear this could be the end of an era.

They face all three of their divisional rivals over the next three weeks.

'Ran through me' & 'good value in pub' - ex-NFL star Kelce tries rugby

After last week's last-gasp win over the Eagles, it was a role reversal for the Jacksonville Jaguars as they remained in London to face the Houston Texans.

The divisional match-up produced the highest-scoring London game since 2015, with Ka'imi Fairbairn's field goal securing a 34-31 win for Houston, but it was a landmark day for Jacksonville's Travis Hunter.

The second overall draft pick in 2025, Hunter came into the league determined to become its first full-time two-way player in 30 years and in his 13th NFL game, he made a significant impact on both offence and defence for the first time.

The 23-year-old, who plays as a wide receiver and cornerback, became the first player to claim a touchdown catch and an interception in the same game since Brian Dawkins (Philadelphia Eagles) in 2002 – and the fourth since the league merger in 1970.

Hunter made both plays in the fourth quarter, with his pick leading to a Cam Little field goal which made it 31-31, before Fairbairn clinched Houston's second win of the season while the Jags slipped to 4-2.

The Draft 'unicorn' that NFL teams just can't figure out

The Baltimore Ravens had a divisional clash at the Cleveland Browns and star running back Derrick Henry had a crucial fumble in the fourth quarter.

That allowed Cleveland running back Audric Estime, who started the week on Minnesota's practice squad, to punch in a touchdown before Andre Szmyt's second game-winning field goal in three weeks gave the Browns a 13-10 victory.

After being booed by Cleveland fans in pre-season, quarterback Deshaun Watson has now led the Browns to a 4-2 start and they are surprise leaders of the AFC North on a tie-breaker.

Baltimore and the Pittsburgh Steelers are also 4-2, with the Steelers having come back from 16-3 down in the fourth quarter to win 26-19 in overtime at the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Next up for Cleveland is a trip to the Tennessee Titans, who fought back in the final quarter to beat the Indianapolis Colts 26-20 for their first victory of the season.

That means the only teams without a win are the Miami Dolphins (0-5) and the Los Angeles Chargers (0-6).

articles.title: Travis Kelce injury news: Andy Reid reveals latest after Chiefs tight end limps off against Chargers
articles.summary: Travis Kelce gave the Kansas City Chiefs a brief injury scare during their 22-6 win over the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday, but Andy Reid’s postgame
articles.body: Travis Kelce gave the Kansas City Chiefs a brief injury scare during their 22-6 win over the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday, but Andy Reid’s postgame update offered some relief. The veteran tight end tweaked his ankle early in the contest, limped off for medical attention and had the area wrapped before returning to action. He finished the game rather than sitting out the remainder, leaving Kansas City with a more encouraging picture than the initial moment suggested. Reid expects Kelce to feel sore, but the coach did not indicate that the injury was a major concern.Travis Kelce injury news: Andy Reid expects the Chiefs star to be soreAndy Reid addressed Travis Kelce’s condition after the victory, confirming that the tight end had played through the ankle problem.“Travis Kelce tweaked his ankle and played through it. Says he’ll be sore tomorrow, but he’ll be OK,” Reid said, according to AotZ Sports reporter Charles Goldman.The update followed a worrying sequence early in the game. After a tackle involving Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley, Kelce left the field and received attention from the Chiefs’ medical staff. His ankle was wrapped, prompting questions about whether he could continue.He returned and remained involved in the offense. Kelce caught four of his five targets for 53 yards, giving Patrick Mahomes another reliable option as Kansas City maintained control of the game.That production matters beyond the box score. Kelce remains a central part of the Chiefs’ passing attack, particularly when Mahomes needs a trusted target in the middle of the field. Losing him during a game would force Kansas City to adjust its plans, even if the offense has other options.For now, Reid’s comments point to soreness rather than a confirmed serious injury. The coach’s assessment is encouraging, although Kelce’s recovery over the next few days will offer a clearer indication of how the ankle responds.Travis Kelce’s return gives Kansas City reason for optimismKelce’s ability to return was the most useful development for the Chiefs. The initial sight of him limping off naturally raised concerns, but his subsequent involvement showed that he could still contribute despite the discomfort.At 37, the veteran is in his 14th NFL season, and managing physical wear becomes an important part of sustaining his role. An ankle tweak does not automatically mean an extended absence, but the Chiefs will want to avoid turning a manageable issue into a lingering problem.Kansas City also has little reason to take unnecessary risks with a key offensive player if his ankle needs additional rest. The next assessment will help determine whether Kelce can continue without restrictions or needs a lighter workload.His return against the Chargers was encouraging, but it should not be mistaken for a full medical clearance for the next game. Reid has offered a positive initial assessment, and there is no indication in his comments that Kelce faces a lengthy layoff.The Chiefs can take comfort in the result and Kelce’s ability to finish Sunday’s contest. articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes got win number 100 on Sunday, October 18, and it came in his 131st start.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes got win number 100 on Sunday, October 18, and it came in his 131st start. That ties him with Tom Brady for the fewest starts to reach the mark. The Kansas City Chiefs beat the visiting Los Angeles Chargers 22-6 at Arrowhead Stadium to move to 5-0 coming out of their bye week. Mahomes threw for 272 yards and an interception, but Kenneth Walker III ran for 128 yards and two touchdowns. Brady’s name came up right away in the on-field interview, and Mahomes had a quick answer ready.Patrick Mahomes ties Tom Brady for fastest 100 winsThe record is simple on paper. Patrick Mahomes needed 131 starts to win 100 games, the same number Brady needed. ESPN Insights put it plainly: “In good company! Patrick Mahomes ties Tom Brady for the fewest starts (131) to reach 100 wins!”There is a catch. Mahomes can only match it now. Every win from here adds to his total, but the starts number is locked at 131.The win rate stands out more. Mahomes has lost only 31 of those starts, which is a win rate near 76 percent. He is doing that while still searching for consistency after his ACL injury, according to Pro Football Network.CBS Sports reporter Melanie Collins asked him about the tie on the field. Mahomes did not wave it off. “I mean, it’s awesome. Because, I mean, he’s the GOAT, man,” Mahomes said. “He’s the one that has kinda shown us how to do it in winning the Super Bowls and winning every single week. So it’s always an honor if you’re mentioned in his name. But it seems like every time I win a game, I’m tying him, so I’m gonna keep winning.”Andy Reid has coached Mahomes through every one of those starts, and his take was drier. “We’re lucky to have him, right? We all know that. We’re lucky to have him. He does a heck of a job playing. 100 wins. He’s going to have a lot more than that down the road,” Reid said.Kenneth Walker leads Chiefs past ChargersThis was not a Patrick Mahomes showcase. He completed 23 of 30 passes for 272 yards and one interception, and added 16 yards on five carries.Walker did the loud work. He ran 19 times for 128 yards and two touchdowns, and caught two passes for 11 more.The receiver room was thin. Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton were both out with injuries, so Xavier Worthy led the group with seven catches for 73 yards. Travis Kelce had four for 53, even after a brief exit in the first half with an ankle injury, which came on an apparent hip-drop tackle by a Chargers linebacker.Rice has been dealing with a hamstring injury since Week 4, and the bye week bought him extra rest. His status for the next game is still unclear.That next game is Sunday Night Football at Seattle, the defending Super Bowl champions. Walker was the Super Bowl MVP for the Seahawks, so he will see old teammates across the field. The injury happened in a split second.The next moment, he was carted off on a stretcher in the third quarter of Sunday’s game against the Chicago Bears.What happened to Kendal Daniels?Kendal Daniels was stumbling, and his head was down. He lost his balance or dove forward awkwardly as he went too low to wrap his arms around Chicago Bears tight end Colston Loveland. His low-lying tackle attempt landed his head on Loveland’s knee.The front grill of his helmet slammed directly into Loveland’s hard, moving knee. The impact was so powerful that the force of the helmet-to-knee hit severely jolted Daniels’ neck. He fell to the ground. He then immediately rolled onto his stomach, face down on the turf. He was in intense pain and unable to move safely.The distressing scene prompted emotional responses from players on both the teams - Atlanta Falcons and the Chicago Bears. Everyone gathered on the gridiron to show support for him.Kevin Stefanski complimented the medical staffMedical personnel arrived at the location where Kendal Daniels was down with pain. He remained motionless for several minutes as medical personnel attended to him.They stabilized his neck and body before loading him into a gurney. They carted him off on a stretcher in the third quarter of the Bears vs. Falcons game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium.On the way off the field, he made a fist with his hand. “He said, ‘Y’all go finish this off.’ He was in good spirits,” Falcons QB Michael Penix Jr. said.Kendal Daniels was alert and conscious, with movement in his extremities. He was taken to Grady Memorial Hospital for further evaluation. He was seen walking in his own power in the locker room after the game.Atlanta Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski told reporters that Daniels’ reports were good. He had movement in his extremities on the field. articles.title: "I wasn't doing what was falsely claimed": Travis Kelce called $3.3 million charity donation report nonsense after fake news went viral
articles.summary: In 2025, Travis Kelce found himself at the centre of an unexpected controversy after reports claimed the Kansas City Chiefs star had donated $3.3 million
articles.body: In 2025, Travis Kelce found himself at the centre of an unexpected controversy after reports claimed the Kansas City Chiefs star had donated $3.3 million to help homeless young people. The story spread quickly across social media, with fans praising the NFL tight end for his reported generosity. However, Kelce has now challenged those claims, making it clear that the donation was not what online reports suggested. His response has also raised questions about the growing influence of unverified stories and AI-generated content, especially when they involve high-profile athletes and their charitable work.Travis Kelce addresses the $3.3 million charity donation claimLast year, Kelce addressed the controversy during the an episode of his New Heights podcast, which he co-hosts with his brother, Jason Kelce. Rather than allowing the rumour to continue unchecked, the Chiefs star urged listeners to question what they see online."I gotta make a little statement in the don't-believe-everything-you-read-kids category, realm that you see online. Some false claims were thrown out there that I was doing something in the community that I was not," Kelce said during the episode. "I'm not even going to talk about it specifically, I don't want to bring any more attention to that whole nonsense and article and all that stuff."The tight end also directed fans towards his official charitable organisation, 87 & Running, for accurate information about his community work."But if you ever want to know exactly what I'm doing in the community, just go to 87 & Running.org," he said, referring to his official non-profit organization. "We're always trying to get out there, get in the Kansas City communities, in the Cleveland community, but this time, I wasn't doing what was falsely claimed by the social channels or outlets posting all this AI stuff."Kelce also acknowledged ESPN personality Pat McAfee, who had praised him as a "good human" while discussing the reported donation. The NFL star thanked McAfee for his support but clarified that the underlying claim was false."So just wanted to set the record straight, appreciate everybody for always trying to show — especially Pat McAfee, he's always trying to look out for the guys, guys and women in the sports world."What happened to the reported Foster Love donation?The original report claimed that Kelce had donated $3.3 million to Foster Love to help establish a facility for young homeless people in Kansas City. According to the Daily Mail, the charity had announced the contribution on social media.However, the New York Post reported that the social media announcement had since disappeared, along with a related story on Foster Love's website. The charity had also not immediately responded to a request for comment.Kelce founded 87 & Running in 2015 to support disadvantaged young people. The organisation focuses on education, business, athletics, STEM and the arts, helping young people access resources and opportunities in their communities.By directing fans to his nonprofit, Kelce made one point clear: people should verify charitable claims before sharing them. articles.title: Terry Bradshaw overcame two cancer diagnoses, but the NFL legend’s latest admission reveals a deeper fear
articles.summary: Terry Bradshaw is cancer-free, but he says he has never been more afraid.
articles.body: Terry Bradshaw is cancer-free, but he says he has never been more afraid. The 78-year-old Hall of Fame quarterback beat early-stage bladder cancer in 2021 and a rare skin cancer in 2022. Every follow-up scan still shakes him. Bradshaw and his wife, Tammy, opened up to PEOPLE this week about both diagnoses, the treatment and the choice to go public. The couple say faith and family got them through, along with what Bradshaw calls courage. He also works as a Fox NFL Sunday analyst. The talk coincides with his new memoir, Looking for Terry.Terry Bradshaw is more scared now than at diagnosisBradshaw says the fear has grown since treatment ended. He still gets recurring scans, and both he and Tammy are “so nervous” every time.“I’m not going to lie to you,” he says, “I’m waiting on it to return.” Adds the four-time Super Bowl champion, “Seriously, I am more scared now than I was the day I found out I had cancer.”Doctors have told him he is cancer-free. Tammy still finds that hard to accept. “It’s hard to trust it, isn’t it?” she says.Many survivors describe the wait between scans as its own kind of strain. Bradshaw is saying it out loud, which stands out from a man known for loud, easy confidence on television.Fear is not the whole story, though. “I’ll tell you what I have. I have courage,” he affirms.How the two diagnoses unfoldedThe first diagnosis came in November 2021. Bradshaw had noticed increased urination, and testing turned up a spot that needed a biopsy. Tammy remembers the doctor saying, “We’ve caught it very, very early. We can do the treatment. Everything should be fine.” He was treated with Bacille Calmette-Guérin immunotherapy.The second cancer was harder. Four months later, in March 2022, neck pain led to the discovery of a 2.5-centimeter tumor on his parotid gland. It was Merkel cell carcinoma, a rare and aggressive skin cancer.Tammy, a former radiology manager, gave him the news herself. Her years in radiation therapy helped her view his health from a “clinical standpoint.” Still, “I was really scared on that one. It was really hard,” she admits. She told him it was treatable, and that “statistically, it’s treatable, and it is statistically possible to cure it, but we’re going to have to really fight hard on this one.”Bradshaw had surgery, then radiation, a “tough treatment,” Tammy notes.Why Bradshaw decided to go publicThe couple first wanted to keep both cancers private. That changed in September 2022 on Fox NFL Sunday. “We were doing a demonstration on the Fox pregame show ... and I couldn’t breathe, and I had to grab [co-host] Howie [Long] to stand up,” Bradshaw recounts. Viewers saw a veteran analyst struggle on air, so staying quiet was no longer realistic. He shared the news that October.It was not for “sympathy,” he insists. “If anything, I want your prayers.”Tammy says they feel “pretty lucky” overall. Her support puts everything in perspective for Bradshaw: “I never thought I’d find this. I heard about this before, but I never thought.” His memoir also covers the highs and lows of his football career and his lifelong clinical depression.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jim Nantz tried to 'peanut punch' JJ Watt and it didn't go well: 'My wrist is broken'
articles.summary: JJ Watt called for some ice for his partner during the next commercial break.
articles.body:
The best sports broadcasters are the ones capable of teaching fans something new and insightful about the game. Jim Nantz and JJ Watt did exactly that Sunday, and it ended in disaster for one of them.

The incident came near the end of the second quarter during the Buffalo Bills' 33-30 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. During a break in the action, Watt decided to teach viewers how to protect the football from a "peanut punch." The camera cut to the booth, where Watt showed off the proper grip players are utilizing to make sure they don't fumble when another player tries to punch the football out of their hands.

Watt then told Nantz to try and punch the ball out of Watt's hands. Nantz took a harder swing than either man expected, and paid the price for it.

Nantz immediately winced after full-on punching the football, which didn't move. Watt started laughing right away, saying he didn't expect Nantz to "go that hard." Nantz took a few moments to gather himself before quipping, "My wrist is broken." He then lamented ever trying to punch the ball out of the hands of a future NFL Hall of Famer. As the game went to a commercial break, Watt joked about getting Nantz some ice for his wrist.

The "peanut punch" is a technique popularized by former Chicago Bears cornerback Charles Tillman, whose nickname was Peanut. Over his 13-year NFL career, Tillman caused 44 fumbles thanks to the technique, which simply involves punching the ball out of your opponent's hands. It was so effective that other players started using it, and it remains a popular technique today.

The "peanut punch" has become such a concern for opposing ballcarriers that they've come up with their own countermeasures to the strategy. Turns out, it's a pretty effective move, as Nantz learned the hard way Sunday.

articles.title: Cris Collinsworth delivers blunt reaction to Tua Tagovailoa’s costly interception
articles.summary: Jean_Nelson/Depositphotos Collinsworth’s reaction follows Baltimore’s overtime win Cris Collinsworth’s reaction to Tua Tagovailoa’s costly interception becam...
articles.body:
Collinsworth's reaction follows Baltimore's overtime win

Cris Collinsworth's reaction to Tua Tagovailoa's costly interception became a talking point after the Baltimore Ravens defeated the Atlanta Falcons 30-23 in overtime on October 11, 2026. The game featured a late comeback by Baltimore, an injury to Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix Jr. and a decisive defensive play by Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton.

Tagovailoa's interception ended Atlanta's chance to respond, while Collinsworth's audible laughter drew attention to the NBC broadcast.

Kyle Hamilton secured Baltimore's victory

Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton intercepted Tagovailoa's pass on Atlanta's final possession of the overtime period. The turnover stopped the Falcons' attempt to answer Baltimore's touchdown and secured the Ravens' 30-23 win.

Hamilton's interception was the decisive defensive play in a contest that had reached overtime after Atlanta lost its lead late in regulation. The Ravens improved to 4-1, while the Falcons fell to 2-3 after the nationally televised matchup.

Michael Penix Jr.'s injury changed Atlanta's plans

Michael Penix Jr. was Atlanta's starting quarterback against Baltimore but sustained a rib injury late in the fourth quarter. He initially missed one snap before returning briefly, but he could not continue into overtime, forcing the Falcons to turn to Tagovailoa.

Penix had been recovering from a torn anterior cruciate ligament that kept him out of Atlanta's first two games of the 2026 season. His late exit changed the quarterback situation at a critical point, leaving Tagovailoa to lead the offense during overtime.

Tagovailoa entered during a high-pressure moment

Tagovailoa made his first regular-season appearance for Atlanta when Penix briefly left the game late in the fourth quarter. He then took over for overtime after Penix could not return.

Tagovailoa completed his first 2 passes for 34 yards before Hamilton intercepted his third attempt. He finished 2-for-3 with no touchdowns and 1 interception as Baltimore secured the victory.

Atlanta held a late lead before Baltimore mounted a scoring drive in the final minute of regulation. Backup quarterback Tyler Huntley completed a 7-yard touchdown pass to Devontez Walker with 40 seconds remaining, bringing the Ravens within 2 points.

Running back Derrick Henry then converted a two-point attempt to tie the score at 23-23. Atlanta could not regain the lead before regulation ended, sending the game to overtime and setting up Baltimore's eventual comeback victory.

Tyler Huntley stepped up without Lamar Jackson

Baltimore entered the matchup without starting quarterback Lamar Jackson, making Huntley's performance especially important to the offense. Huntley completed 24 of 32 passes for 201 yards and 2 passing touchdowns while helping the Ravens recover from their late deficit.

He also ran for a 1-yard touchdown in overtime, giving Baltimore the lead. The Ravens then secured the 30-23 victory when Hamilton intercepted Tagovailoa's pass, completing the comeback despite Jackson's absence from the lineup.

Tagovailoa's pass went directly to Hamilton

The interception came when Tagovailoa attempted to throw toward Falcons receiver Drake London during overtime. Hamilton was positioned to make the play, intercepted the pass and ended Atlanta's possession before the offense could produce a tying score.

The turnover was especially consequential because Baltimore had already scored on its opening overtime drive. With Hamilton securing possession, the Falcons could not answer the Ravens' touchdown, and the game ended with Baltimore winning by seven points.

Interesting fact : Cris Collinsworth was a three-time Pro Bowl wide receiver for the Cincinnati Bengals, finishing his eight-season NFL career with 417 receptions and 36 touchdowns.

Collinsworth's laughter became a separate storyline

Collinsworth's audible laughter after the interception became a subject of postgame coverage. Sports Illustrated reported on his reaction during the NBC broadcast, while other sports outlets covered Hamilton's game-ending interception.

The moment prompted discussion about how broadcasters react to decisive mistakes during live games. Although the interception itself ended the contest, Collinsworth's response added a broadcast angle to coverage of Baltimore's 30-23 overtime victory.

The Falcons missed a chance to improve their record

Atlanta entered Week 5 looking to build momentum during the 2026 NFL season. Instead, the overtime defeat left the Falcons with a 2-3 record, while Baltimore improved to 4-1 after winning its fourth game of the campaign.

The loss was particularly difficult because Atlanta had held the advantage late in regulation. Baltimore's final-minute touchdown, successful two-point conversion and overtime score changed the outcome and prevented the Falcons from securing the home victory.

Tagovailoa arrived in Atlanta after leaving Miami

Tagovailoa spent his first 6 NFL seasons with Miami after the Dolphins selected him fifth overall in 2020. He signed a 1-year contract with Atlanta in March 2026 to compete with Michael Penix Jr.

By the Baltimore game, Tagovailoa was serving as Penix's backup. His relief appearance marked his first regular-season action for the Falcons, ending with the overtime interception that secured the Ravens' victory.

Penix's rib injury initially raised questions about his availability after Atlanta's overtime loss to Baltimore. He returned to practice during the following week and was cleared to start against Chicago.

Penix played in Atlanta's October 18 game, completing 19 of 33 passes for 225 yards and 3 touchdowns. The Falcons lost 31–23 to the Bears, falling to 2–4.

The Ravens' defense delivered at the decisive moment

Baltimore's defense prevented Atlanta from extending its possession after the Ravens took the lead in overtime. Hamilton's interception finished the game and ensured that Huntley's touchdown would stand as the winning score in the 30-23 result.

The play capped a comeback in which Baltimore erased Atlanta's late advantage and tied the score before regulation expired. Hamilton's contribution also highlighted the importance of defensive turnovers in close games, particularly when an opponent is trying to recover from an overtime deficit.

A dramatic finish gave the broadcast its closing moment

Baltimore's October 11 comeback brought together Huntley's late scoring drives and Hamilton's decisive interception. Collinsworth's audible laugh added another memorable moment to the finish, drawing attention alongside the Ravens' 30–23 overtime victory.

Atlanta returned to action with Penix starting against Chicago on October 18, but lost 31–23. After Week 6, the Falcons stood at 2–4 and the Ravens at 4–2.

articles.title: Panthers’ JJ Jansen makes history, plays 282nd game, most ever for a long snapper
articles.summary: Carolina Panthers long snapper JJ Jansen is set to make history on Sunday when he plays in his 282nd NFL game.
articles.body:
Carolina Panthers long snapper JJ Jansen made history on Sunday when he played in his 282nd NFL game.

The Panthers faced the Philadelphia Eagles.

The appearance set a new NFL record for the most games played by a long snapper, surpassing Trey Junkin's previous record.

Jansen, 40, was a long snapper for Notre Dame before joining the Green Bay Packers as an undrafted free agent in 2008, where he only participated in preseason play and spent the regular season on injured reserve.

The Panthers acquired Jansen in 2009, and he has remained in Carolina ever since.

Among active players in the league, Jansen ranks second in total games played behind Calais Campbell, a defensive end for the Baltimore Ravens who has appeared in 283 games.

Former Detroit Lions kicker Jason Hanson holds the NFL record for the most games played for a single franchise at 327 games.

articles.title: Commanders LB K'Lavon Chaisson still believes Commanders can win Super Bowl
articles.summary: Washington Commanders linebacker K'Lavon Chaisson still believes the Commanders can win the Super Bowl this year despite starting the year 1-3-1.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders sit at the bottom of the NFC East with a 1-3-1 record after an embarrassing tie with the New York Giants and will face one of the Super Bowl favorites on Monday night. Even so, they still believe they can win the Super Bowl.

"I think the full belief is there. I was talking to the guys, and obviously, you want to go one week at a time and focus on that," linebacker K'Lavon Chaisson said. "But, 13-3-1 is a weird Super Bowl-winning record, but, s***, we'll take it. Whatever it takes to get there. So, continues this just one week at a time and focus on San Fran and clean up the self-inflicted wounds on ourselves and I feel we'll be in good position for sure."

It may seem crazy to think this team will win the Super Bowl after the first five weeks. But, crazier things have happened. More importantly, Washington is still easily in the mix for the NFC East title. New York is currently first and has the only winning record in the division. The Dallas Cowboys and Philadelphia Eagles are 2-4, although the Eagles' season appears to be in shambles due to injuries.

Washington has dealt with numerous injuries as well, but at least they have starting quarterback Jayden Daniels back. Getting a win against the San Francisco 49ers on Monday night would put the NFL on notice that the Commanders are not going anywhere and are still playoff contenders despite how this season started for them. Washington's lone win of the season so far is against the reigning Super Bowl champions, the Seattle Seahawks , so they are capable of handing the 49ers their first loss of the year.

articles.title: Detroit Lions Get Major Josh Jacobs News Ahead of Packers Showdown
articles.summary: Josh Jacobs is eligible to return for the Packers' Week 7 game against the Detroit Lions after the NFL removes him from the exempt list.
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions could be facing a much more dangerous Green Bay Packers offense than originally expected when the two NFC North rivals meet Sunday at Ford Field. Star running back Josh Jacobs is officially eligible to return for Week 7 after spending the first six weeks of the season on the NFL's Commissioner Exempt List.

The NFL announced that Jacobs would be removed from the exempt list on Monday, October 19 , clearing the way for the three-time Pro Bowler to potentially make his season debut against Detroit. Although his availability for Sunday's game has not been confirmed, the development gives Green Bay an opportunity to regain one of its most important offensive weapons.

The timing is significant for Dan Campbell and the Lions, who are coming off their bye week following a dominant 45-21 victory over the Arizona Cardinals. Detroit now faces a critical divisional showdown against a Packers team that improved to 4-2 with Sunday night's 23-13 victory over Dallas.

NFL Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs. Mandatory Credit: Scott Galvin-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Josh Jacobs Could Give Packers Major Boost Against Lions

Jacobs has not appeared in a regular-season game this year after being placed on the Commissioner's Exempt List on August 30. The designation followed a legal case stemming from a May incident involving his former girlfriend, for which Jacobs pleaded no contest to misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property charges.

The NFL's investigation under its Personal Conduct Policy remains ongoing, meaning additional discipline has not been ruled out. However, the league's latest decision makes Jacobs eligible to practice and potentially play against Detroit.

According to additional reporting on Green Bay's running back situation , the Packers have struggled to generate consistent rushing production during Jacobs' absence. Through their first five games, MarShawn Lloyd had rushed for just 112 yards, while Kaleb Johnson had added 106.

That's a significant drop-off from what Jacobs provided Green Bay in previous seasons. After rushing for 1,329 yards and 15 touchdowns in 2024, the veteran followed with 929 yards and 13 touchdowns in 2025.

His potential return would give quarterback Jordan Love another proven weapon and could force Detroit to devote additional attention to Green Bay's rushing attack. But because Jacobs has been unable to participate in normal team practices during his absence, the Packers must still determine whether he is ready for game action.

Detroit Lions Face Growing Challenge Against Green Bay

The Jacobs development comes as Green Bay's offense appears to be finding its rhythm. Love threw for 276 yards in Sunday's win over Dallas, helping the Packers extend their winning streak to three games.

As we previously reported , the Packers have also suffered significant defensive losses, including season-ending Achilles injuries to Javon Hargrave and Edgerrin Cooper. That could create opportunities for Jared Goff and Detroit's offense, even if Jacobs makes Green Bay more dangerous on the other side of the football.

The Lions have their own personnel questions to answer, particularly regarding the health of their secondary. As we previously highlighted , Brian Branch and Cade Mays have been working toward potential returns following extended injury absences.

For Detroit, the immediate concern is preparing for a Green Bay offense that could feature Jacobs alongside Love and the Packers' receiving weapons. Even if Jacobs plays a limited role, his presence could change how the Lions approach defending the run and play-action passing game.

The biggest takeaway is that Josh Jacobs is now eligible to face the Detroit Lions, but his participation has not been guaranteed. Sunday's matchup kicks off at 4:25 p.m. ET at Ford Field, with FOX carrying the NFC North showdown.
