articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers star receiver DK Metcalf didn't have much sympathy for head coach Mike McCarthy after his ankle injury in Sunday's win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers star receiver DK Metcalf didn't have much sympathy for head coach Mike McCarthy after his ankle injury in Sunday's win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Per The Athletic's Michael Silver , McCarthy said after the game that he was stepped on at the end of the second quarter and had to get treatment on his foot and ankle during halftime. However, Metcalf didn't feel sorry for him.

"Tape that s--t and come on, bro," wide receiver DK Metcalf said to ESPN's Jeff Darlington after the game, while flashing a highly skeptical facial expression, per Silver.

McCarthy coached the rest of the game from the sideline and helped the Steelers earn a 26-19 win in overtime.

McCarthy will try to avoid further mishaps when the Steelers (4-2) face the New Orleans Saints (2-4) in the NFL Paris Game in Week 7.

articles.title: Colts Fire GM Chris Ballard After Loss to Titans, Top Replacements for Carlie Irsay-Gordon's Team
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts announced Monday they fired general manager Chris Ballard.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts announced Monday they fired general manager Chris Ballard.

"I am grateful to Chris for his years of service to the Colts and for everything he poured into this organization," team owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon said . "He cared deeply about our team and our community, and we wish Chris and his family all the best.

"As I said at the start of the season, the sense of urgency has never been higher. Our standard is to compete for championships, and I believe a change in leadership is necessary to meet that standard."

The move comes after the Colts lost 26-20 to the previously winless Tennessee Titans to fall to 2-4 on the season.

Given the timing of the change, Indianapolis will presumably wait until the offseason to name a permanent replacement for Ballard.

Back in January, The MMQB's Albert Breer listed off front-office executives who were potentially climbing up to a general manager job. Among those included was Colts assistant GM Ed Dodds, so Irsay-Gordon may not have to look far.

Detroit Lions general manager Ray Agnew, Kansas City Chiefs assistant general manager Mike Bradway and Buffalo Bills assistant general manager Terrance Gray were some of the others cited by Breer.

For some, Ballard's dismissal is long overdue.

The Colts have gone 72-82-1 and have one lone playoff win since he arrived in January 2017. They've missed the postseason altogether for five straight seasons.

Ballard got to hire two different head coaches (Frank Reich and Shane Steichen). Reich got the boot midway through the 2022 season, and Steichen doesn't look to be the answer on the sideline, either.

Indy has cycled through multiple starting quarterbacks as well and appears to have whiffed badly on Anthony Richardson, the No. 4 overall pick in 2023. Richardson has logged a total of 17 appearances since arriving in the NFL.

Signing Daniel Jones to a two-year, $88 million contract is quickly becoming an expensive mistake as he's regressing after his return from a major Achilles injury.

The decision to keep Steichen while firing Ballard is a sign Irsay-Gordon believes there's time to turn the season around. Maybe she's right.

But the Miami Dolphins made the same calculation last year when they dismissed general manager Chris Grier on Halloween. Head coach Mike McDaniel eventually followed him out the door in January after Miami finished 7-10.

If the Colts' playoff drought stretches to six years, ownership could decide to wipe the slate totally clean rather than retain Steichen with a new GM for 2027.

articles.title: Dalton Signs Falcons Contract After Eagles Exit amid Tua & Penix Injury Concerns, NFL Rumors Reveal
articles.summary: The Atlanta Falcons have been dealing with injury concerns at the quarterback position throughout the year, so they've reportedly added some veteran help.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons have been dealing with injury concerns at the quarterback position throughout the year, so they've reportedly added some veteran help.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , the Falcons are signing quarterback Andy Dalton to be the backup behind Michael Penix Jr. and Tua Tagovailoa. Atlanta released veteran backup Cooper Rush in a corresponding move.

Dalton started the season with the Philadelphia Eagles before being released earlier this month. He briefly replaced Jalen Hurts in Week 3 and threw an interception on his lone pass attempt.

Rush opened the 2026 season as Atlanta's starter while Penix and Tagovailoa recovered from knee and oblique injuries, respectively. The Falcons have kept four quarterbacks on the roster for the entire year along with undrafted rookie Jack Strand.

Penix suffered a rib injury in Atlanta's Week 5 loss to the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday Night Football , which forced Tagovailoa into action. The 28-year-old threw a game-ending interception in overtime.

In Sunday's matchup against the Chicago Bears, Penix managed to play the whole game and threw three touchdown passes for his first multi-score game of the season. However, the Falcons suffered a 31-23 loss and fell to 2-4. Penix briefly visited the medical tent but downplayed any concerns after the game, telling reporters , "I did go into the injury tent. I'm not going to say what that was about. Just say I am good."

The Falcons will try to avoid further injury concerns and end their two-game skid when they face the San Francisco 49ers (5-0) in Week 7.

articles.title: Week 7 Waiver Wire Pickups Highlighted by Germie Bernard, Omar Cooper Jr., Tre Tucker
articles.summary: One note for all of the fantasy managers who will soon work the waiver wire ahead of Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season: Hopefully you're in need of a pass-catcher.
articles.body:
One note for all of the fantasy managers who will soon work the waiver wire ahead of Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season: Hopefully you're in need of a pass-catcher.

While there are still some interesting options available in shallower leagues at quarterback (Kirk Cousins) and running back (Zach Charbonnet), wide receiver sits head and shoulders above the other positions in terms of potential impact among widely available players.

To help hammer that point home, let's dissect three receivers who are available in 50-plus percent of leagues (per FantasyPros ) and should be waiver-wire priority pickups this week.

Germie Bernard, WR, Pittsburgh Steelers (35% Rostered)

Fantasy managers probably should have picked up Bernard already last week, as his six-reception, 80-yard effort in Week 5 felt like an indication of bigger days to come.

The good news is managers have a second chance to correct this oversight. The urgent news is that those same managers almost certainly won't get a third crack at this.

Bernard was awesome in all ways fantasy managers could hope on Sunday. He saw a huge amount of opportunities (12 targets), made the most of those chances (11 receptions for 87 yards) and found his way to the end zone (one touchdown). The Steelers gave him a chance to show what he could do, and he seized the heck out of this moment.

Pittsburgh, which won both of Bernard's big outings, has no reason to rethink this strategy of upping the rookie second-rounder's involvement. So, again, you better act now, because his rostership should be rocketing up.

Omar Cooper Jr., WR, New York Jets (14% Rostered)

Only three words are needed to accurately sum up the Sunday showing by Cooper: worth the wait.

The rookie first-rounder returned from a four-game absence with an ankle injury and immediately looked like he was doing everything he could to make up for that lost time. He turned his team-high seven targets into six receptions for 103 yards and a score.

No other New York pass-catcher managed even 50 receiving yards.

While Garrett Wilson remains WR1 for the Jets, Cooper has a real shot at earning the WR2 role, at least until Adonai Mitchell returns from his finger injury. And if Cooper remains as productive as he was on Sunday, he might be heavily involved in the passing game plan regardless who lines up around him.

Tre Tucker, WR, Las Vegas Raiders (47% Rostered)

This maybe wasn't Bingo card-material in the preseason, but the Raiders boast one of the NFL's most prolific passing attacks. Quarterback Kirk Cousins is tied for the league lead with 14 touchdown passes, and his 1,582 passing yards rank fifth-most overall.

In other words, volume in this passing attack could carry a lot of fantasy-relevance. And Tucker is seeing more than enough volume to matter.

His 35 targets pace all Raiders receivers, and he just had his second monster effort of the season on Sunday. He hauled in five of his seven targets and turned them into 97 yards and two scores. He also had a 119-yard, one-score performance back in Week 2, so be careful about dismissing the performance as an anomalous flash in the pan.

Cousins sees legendary speed in Tucker and sounds eager to keep exploring this connection with downfield targets. Having the trust of a passer who is this productive could deliver season-long results.

articles.title: Schottenheimer, Dak Take Blame After Cowboys Lose to Packers, 'Mistakes are Killing Us'
articles.summary: After losing to the Green Bay Packers on Sunday Night Football and falling to 2-4, the Dallas Cowboys are left searching for answers.
articles.body:
After losing to the Green Bay Packers on Sunday Night Football and falling to 2-4, the Dallas Cowboys are left searching for answers.

Per The Athletic's Jon Machota , Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer and quarterback Dak Prescott shouldered the blame for the team's poor start to the 2026 campaign.

"I'm going to just start with what I told the guys," Schottenheimer said. "The effort is right. The fight is right. But mistakes are killing us. Repeating mistakes is not what we're about. We got to clean it up. Lost two games in a row. Haven't played well. And got to take a hard look at it. And that starts with me."

The Cowboys struggled to get anything going offensively in their 23-13 loss to a Packers team that was without stars Micah Parsons, Edgerrin Cooper and Javon Hargrave. It was the second straight week that Dallas failed to crack the 20-point mark, a far cry from what was expected of one of the most skilled offensive units in the league.

"We got to figure that out," Prescott said of their offensive struggles. "I wish I could give you that answer at this time. (I have to) watch the film to see what wasn't done or what wasn't executed efficiently. I know I had plays out there that I want back that I know directly correlated to a turnover and us getting off the field on third down, and fourth down on one of them. I don't have the answer for the whole team and what that is, but I believe in who we are and I know we have the talent and the men that care. We just have to put it together. Our process is right, but we have to win on Sunday."

Prescott threw two interceptions and finished with 258 yards and a touchdown on 34-of-54 passing. The signal-caller now has five interceptions through the first six weeks of the season, already halfway to the 10 picks he threw in all of 2025.

"We're in a hole," Schottenheimer said. "We put ourselves there, and there's one way out of it. That's what I told the guys. I said, you got to work, got to find solutions, can't repeat mistakes. And they understand that."

As Machota noted, how Schottenheimer handles these next few weeks "could be what ultimately determines his future in Dallas." The second-year head coach expressed confidence that his team can bounce back and return to playoff contention this year.

"There's definitely time to pull out of it," he said. "But we got to fix the mistakes that we've talked about. … Go back to work. That's what we're going to do. Division game, Philadelphia (next week), another place that's tough to play at. But our guys are going to respond. It's not the effort, it's the execution. And that's what we got to clean up, and that's as a football team, coaches and players alike."

Prescott echoed that sentiment and had an optimistic outlook on the Cowboys' chances of chasing the NFC East crown, starting with their Monday Night Football clash against the division rival Philadelphia Eagles in Week 7.

"It's about us fixing our issues, cleaning house and just getting better. From there, the division is open, that will take care of itself," Prescott said. "But we have to win first and we have to get going and from there we can try to build. It is about finding a way to win."

articles.title: Latest on Jalen Hurts' Timeline for Eagles Return After Being Placed IR With Blood Clots
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts was placed on injured reserve on Saturday after being diagnosed with blood clots but he is expected to be able to eventually resume football activities in the future, his agent confirmed on Monday, though ESPN's Adam Schefter reports Hurts will miss the remainder of this season:
articles.body:
Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts was placed on injured reserve on Saturday after being diagnosed with blood clots but he is expected to be able to eventually resume football activities in the future, his agent confirmed on Monday, though ESPN's Adam Schefter reports Hurts will miss the remainder of this season:

Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport had previously reported that injured reserve wasn't in the initial plans.

"The team, according to sources, has not even discussed the possibility of IR, which would sideline him for a minimum of four weeks," according to Schefter and Rapoport. "In general, the minimum timeframe for a moderate dose of anticoagulants is six weeks, sources say."

However, after consulting with doctors, that decision changed.

The Eagles released a statement on the situation on Thursday:

"On Thursday, October 8th, Jalen visited the training room after practice requesting treatment for his calf. He informed the medical staff he had been cleated during the Rams game on October 4th. This was his first treatment session for the calf injury following the game, after having practiced in full both Wednesday and Thursday. On Friday, Jalen received treatment, practiced in full, and was added to the practice report.

"Out of an abundance of caution, an ultrasound was performed on Saturday following the team's flight to London and walkthrough. The ultrasound revealed a superficial blood clot. Our medical staff and doctors in London reviewed the results and concluded that activity and mobility were important and that Jalen could safely play. Doctors recommended a follow-up ultrasound within 72 hours of the game and the return flight to Philadelphia.

"Jalen played without limitation in the game Sunday, received treatment on Monday and Tuesday, and practiced in full on Wednesday, as reflected in the practice report. Throughout our time in London and this week, we have remained in communication with the league office regarding the matter.

"On Wednesday night, a follow-up ultrasound revealed movement in the small blood clot. Jalen will be out for Sunday's game vs. the Panthers as we determine the appropriate course of treatment. His health and safety are our highest priority."

Hurts previously dealt with a calf injury that he suffered during a Week 4 matchup with the Los Angeles Rams, but was able to play through it in Philadelphia's loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 5.

Availability hasn't been a major issue for Hurts throughout his career, as he appeared in 48 of a possible 51 games from 2023-25.

This season, the 28-year-old has completed 57.8 percent of his passes for 933 yards, eight touchdowns and three interceptions in five games/

Hurts has also continued to make plays with his legs, rushing for 107 yards and one touchdown.

Philadelphia (3-3) is looking to clinch its sixth consecutive playoff appearance and third straight division crown. After capturing a Super Bowl title during the 2024 season, the Eagles suffered a disappointing elimination in the Wild Card round last year.

With Hurts out, backup passer Tanner McKee filled in for the Eagles in Sunday's loss to the Carolina Panthers.

articles.title: Jalen Hurts Out for Eagles' Season, New NFL Rumors Reveal After Agent's Statement on Blood Clots
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles star quarterback Jalen Hurts will miss the remainder of the 2026 NFL season after doctors diagnosed him with deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.
articles.body:
Philadelphia Eagles star quarterback Jalen Hurts will miss the remainder of the 2026 NFL season after doctors diagnosed him with deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter .

Nicole Lynn, Hurts' agent, announced Monday that doctors prescribed him with blood thinners to remedy his current clotting issues. His physical activity will be significantly limited while he's on the medication:

Tom Pelissero of The Ringer and Netflix reported Hurts played after being awake for nearly 36 hours, as doctors had told him not to sleep. However, Hurts' agent later clarified the report to note that Hurts was able to sleep at the stadium before the game:

Per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , Hurts was in the hospital until 4 a.m.

Rapoport reported the estimated time frame is three months.

Unfortunately for Hurts and the Eagles, injuries have been a big part of the 2026 campaign so far.

After a loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 5, Hurts revealed that he suffered a calf injury the previous week against the Los Angeles Rams. The calf injury clearly limited him, as he threw for 220 yards and a touchdown but managed just two carries for two yards.

Hurts was then ruled out for a Week 6 matchup against the Carolina Panthers after being diagnosed with a superficial blood clot.

In what has been a down year for both him and the Eagles, Hurts recorded 933 passing yards, 107 rushing yards and nine total touchdowns. Philadelphia is sitting at 2-4 on the season after Sunday's 25-14 loss to the Carolina Panthers.

With Hurts set to miss time, the Eagles will have to stick with Tanner McKee as the starter absent another addition to the QB room. McKee went 26-of-45 for 215 yards and a touchdown against the Panthers.

articles.title: Indianapolis Colts fire general manager Chris Ballard following loss to Tennessee Titans that extended poor start to NFL season
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts suffered an upset defeat to the Tennessee Titans in Week Six to fall to 2-4 on the season as they look to end a six-year playoff drought; the Colts reached the playoffs just twice during Chris Ballard's time as General Manager
articles.body:
Ballard was hired as back in 2017 and departs with a record of 72-82-1 having reached the playoffs just twice during his time in charge.

The Colts were beaten 26-20 by the Tennessee Titans in Week Six to fall to 2-4 as they bid to reach the playoffs for the first time since 2020.

Ballard's only playoff win in Indianapolis came in the 2018-19 campaign when the Colts defeated the Houston Texans in the Wild Card round, before being eliminated by the Kansas City Chiefs the following week.

"I am grateful to Chris for his years of service to the Colts and for everything he poured into this organisation. He cared deeply about our team and our community, and we wish Chris and his family all the best," said Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon in a statement.

"As I said at the start of the season, the sense of urgency has never been higher. Our standard is to compete for championships, and I believe a change in leadership is necessary to meet that standard.

"Making this change during the season was a deliberate decision. Waiting would only delay the important work that needs to begin now. We will conduct a thorough search for our next general manager and take the time necessary to identify the right leader for the future of this organisation.

"I also want to be clear: this decision does not change our goals for the season. We have a lot of football in front of us, and I expect us to compete, improve, and win football games."

The Colts had appeared on course to thrust their way among the NFL's perennial contenders in 2018 when Andrew Luck flourished on his way to winning Comeback Player of the Year, while Ballard delivered inspired Draft picks in left guard Quenton Nelson and linebacker Shaquille Leonard.

A defining setback to the Ballard era arrived in 2019 when Luck stunned the NFL by announced his shock retirement, plunging the Colts into quarterback purgatory from which they have never quite recovered.

The Colts cycled through the likes of Jacoby Brissett, Philip Rivers, Carson Wentz and Matt Ryan to little avail under center, while head coach Frank Reich was fired mid-way through the 2022 season to create further uncertainty over the direction of the franchise.

Ballard sought to find his next quarterback of the future at the 2023 NFL Draft when he used the No 4 overall pick on Anthony Richardson, who was unable to translate his sparkling college impact into success on the biggest stage.

His failure to assert himself as a long-term answer under Shane Steichen would pave the way for Daniel Jones to resurrect his career by way of an 8-2 start in 2025, before injuries proved a catalyst for the Colts collapsing out of playoff contention.

Jones was then handed a two-year $88m extension this past offseason, but has struggled upon his return from injury.

Right now not even the influence of offensive heartbeat Jonathan Taylor looks enough to fuel an Indianapolis playoff threat this time. Ultimately, a failure to find the answer at quarterback in life after Luck has cost Ballard.

articles.title: Jayden Daniels, Dan Quinn Hot Seat Addressed by Commanders Players After Tie, New NFL Rumors Reveal
articles.summary: The internal pressure on Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels and coach Dan Quinn hasn't yet ramped up amid a 1-3-1 start to the 2026 NFL season, according to ESPN's John Keim.
articles.body:
The internal pressure on Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels and coach Dan Quinn hasn't yet ramped up amid a 1-3-1 start to the 2026 NFL season, according to ESPN's John Keim .

Keim cited multiple players who indicated "the team has not lost confidence" in Daniels, Quinn or offensive coordinator David Blough after the meltdown in a Week 5 tie with the New York Giants.

The Commanders were well within field-goal range to win the game but never got the special teams unit on the field thanks to some disastrous clock management.

Keim described what happened at the team facility in the aftermath of the disappointing outcome:

"Daniels briefly addressed the offensive players in a meeting last Monday, and one player said some clapped for him. Other teammates seated in the front row — where Daniels always sits — dapped him up after he spoke. The player said it was reminiscent of how they responded to him two weeks prior, when he told them that he'd return from a dislocated left elbow suffered in Week 2. Then, they clapped and cheered loudly. Some even stood, according to multiple people who were in the room.

"Ultimately, Quinn, Blough and Daniels all accepted responsibility for the play -- both to the team and when addressing the media during their respective press conferences this week."

In terms of the bigger picture, Keim reported Quinn's future on the sideline "is not in immediate jeopardy" and that "ownership is aware of the support Quinn has in the locker room."

Appearing on 106.7 The Fan (via The Athletic's Nicki Jhabvala), general manager Adam Peters didn't rule out making a midseason trade to improve the roster:

When it comes to Quinn, the patience of owner Josh Harris may not be infinite. The coach's seat could grow a bit warmer if the losses continue to pile up.

The state of the NFC East is probably helping his job security, though.

The Giants are leading the division at 3-2-1, and they're not inspiring a lot of confidence with Jameis Winston under center. The Philadelphia Eagles are snakebitten with injuries and riding a four-game losing streak. The 2-4 Dallas Cowboys are held back by having one of the league's worst defenses.

All is not lost for the Commanders, and beating the 5-0 San Francisco 49ers on Monday night would be an encouraging sign heading into a Week 7 bye.

articles.title: Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts likely out for season after blood clots found in lungs and leg
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts was diagnosed with blood clots in his lungs and leg, the team said Monday, likely sidelining the Super Bowl MVP for the rest of 2026.
articles.body: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts was diagnosed with blood clots in his lungs and leg, the team said Monday, likely sidelining the Super Bowl MVP for the rest of 2026. Hurts last played Oct. 11, in the Eagles’ 19-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in London before he was kept off the field in Sunday’s 25-14 setback to the visiting Carolina Panthers. Hurts was originally diagnosed with “superficial vein thrombosis” in his left calf, the team said. “After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli,” the statement continued. “He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations.” Both deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE) are forms of venous thromboembolism, commonly known as blood clots in the veins, according to the Centers for Disease Control. DVT is when a blood clot develops in a vein deep within the body, most commonly in the leg, the CDC says. PE happens when pieces of a blood clot from a DVT break off and travel to the veins in the lungs. The clots can prevent blood from reaching the lungs, which can be fatal. He’s being treated with blood thinners and “during this time, he will not be allowed to participate in any contact activities, including football,” according to the Eagles. Hurts was held out of the game on Sunday after the Eagles announced last week a superficial blood clot was found in London ahead of the game against the Jaguars. Despite that diagnosis, Hurts still played the full game in London. “Our medical staff and doctors in London reviewed the results and concluded that activity and mobility were important and that [Hurts] could safely play,” the team said last week, adding that Hurts “played without limitation.” But when a follow-up scan was conducted back in Philadelphia, the team said the superficial blood clot had moved, which prompted them to pull Hurts from the game against the Panthers. Further testing revealed the deep vein clot and the clots in the lungs, leading to Hurts being indefinitely sidelined. The team didn’t set an exact timeline for his return, though action for 2026 seems highly unlikely. A blood thinner treatment can typically last between three months and six months as doctors bring the condition under control and search for any previously undiagnosed, underlying conditions in a patient. And contact sport athletes cannot play while taking blood thinner due to the risk of an uncontrollable, and potentially deadly, bleed from an injury. “We anticipate that he will have no long-term effect,” the club said. Hurts was MVP of Super Bowl 59, leading his team to a 40-22 win over the Kansas City Chiefs on Feb. 9 2025, in New Orleans. The team’s 2026 fortunes now rest in the hands of career backup Tanner McKee, a sixth-round 2023 pick. The 26-year-old Stanford alum comes from the same high school graduation class as current NFL signal callers Brock Purdy of the San Francisco 49ers, Trevor Lawrence of the Jacksonville Jaguars and Will Levis, who is on the practice squad of the New York Jets. Philadelphia won the 2018 Super Bowl with backup QB Nick Foles leading the Birds past Tom Brady’s New England Patriots. The journeyman Foles was the game’s MVP, executing one of football’s most famous trick plays that evening, the “Philly Special.”

articles.title: Peyton Manning Eyed by Colts for GM Job After Chris Ballard Fired, Dan Patrick Reveals in New Video
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard on Monday following the team's 2-4 start to the season.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard on Monday following the team's 2-4 start to the season.

According to Dan Patrick, the Colts are considering former quarterback Peyton Manning for the general manager vacancy and exploring if he would be interested in the position and potentially an ownership stake down the line:

Manning, 50, has long been rumored as a target for NFL teams in either a coaching or executive role, though to this point he's favored a position in media following his playing career. Perhaps a reunion with his first NFL team, in a general manager role, could be the move that sways him.

Either way, the Colts now have a vacancy at an incredibly important position.

"Making this change during the season was a deliberate decision," team owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon said in a statement . "Waiting would only delay the important work that needs to begin now. We will conduct a thorough search for our next general manager and take the time necessary to identify the right leader for the future of this organization. I also want to be clear: this decision does not change our goals for the season. We have a lot of football in front of us, and I expect us to compete, improve, and win football games."

The decision to fire Ballard also means head coach Shane Steichen could be on the hot seat as well following a rough start to the 2026 season. He's just 27-30 in his fourth season on the job and has yet to lead Indy to a playoff appearance.

"Extremely disappointing," Steichen said of Sunday's loss to the previously winless Tennessee Titans. "We've got a lot to fix, and we've got to fix it in a hurry."

"We've got to give them something to cheer about," he added of the fans that booed the team during the 26-20 defeat. "I don't blame them for booing one freaking bit."

Perhaps it will be Manning that ultimately decides Steichen's future. The Hall of Famer would certainly be a splashy addition in the role.

articles.title: Jalen Hurts: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback set to miss rest of NFL season due to blood clots
articles.summary: NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reports that Jalen Hurts will miss the rest of the 2026 NFL season, explaining that Hurts was in hospital until 4am ahead of the Philadelphia Eagles' loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in London in Week Five
articles.body:
The Eagles and Hurts' agent Nicole Lynn released a joint-statement on Monday saying he will be placed on blood thinners and is unable to play football until his recovery.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported that Hurts is out for the rest of the year, adding that the former Super Bowl MVP was in hospital until 4am and did not sleep prior to Philadelphia's defeat to the Jacksonville Jaguars in London.

"Over the past few days, Jalen Hurts has received comprehensive medical evaluations by physician experts. In the interest of transparency, we are providing additional information on the diagnosis and treatment plan related to his condition," the joint-statement read.

"Jalen was initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis. After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations. His treatment should only involve anticoagulation [ie. 'blood thinners']. During this time, he will not be allowed to participate in any contact activities, including football."

The statement adds that a "full recovery" is expected for Hurts and no long-term effects are anticipated.

Hurts started the Eagles' game in London despite not sleeping, throwing for 220 yards and a touchdown before Cam Little's last-second field goal lifted Jacksonville to a 19-17 victory.

Rapoport added that the initial blood clot issue was revealed on the Saturday afternoon to be several blood clots on Hurts' lungs.

Hurts won Super Bowl LIX MVP in February 2025 after throwing for 293 yards and scoring three touchdowns as the Eagles beat the Kansas City Chiefs 40-22 in New Orleans.

Stat Line : 24 of 35 for 218 yards and an interception

In an ironic twist, the Arizona Cardinals didn't need quarterback Jacoby Brissett to throw for 275 or more yards to make a game competitive and secure an upset victory.

For the first time this season, Brissett didn't even throw a touchdown pass. Yet the Cardinals walked away with a stunning victory over the Los Angeles Rams.

The veteran quarterback threw an interception during the Cardinals' initial offensive possession. From that point, Brissett minimized mistakes and allowed the Cardinals defense to keep them in the game.

"We're sustaining drives. We're keeping the other team off the field. I thought the defense played great today," Brissett told reporters . "When you sustain drives, you help them stay rested. They go out there and fire out the ball, and I think they did a really good job. Hats off to them."

During the final drive, the quarterback ripped the contest's most important pass to Jalen Brooks. With an unnecessary roughness tacked onto the play, the Cardinals were within game-winning field goal distance and converted.

Stat Line : 19 of 33 for 225 yards, three touchdowns and a fumble lost

The Chicago Bears devised a very specific gameplan when facing the Atlanta Falcons' Michael Penix Jr. and it involved creating significant pressure.

According to ESPN Research (via Marc Raimondi ), the Bears pressured Penix on a career-high 46 percent of his dropbacks. To Penix's credit, he responded in the second half after being rattled in the first. The quarterback completed eight of 13 passes and connected on two touchdowns when pressured during the third and fourth quarters. But the damage had already been done.

"We just have to come ready to play, and we have to execute," Penix told reporters . "We have to execute the game plan. I always love the game plan we have in. We knew what to expect. It's not like they did too many things that surprised us. We have to go and execute at a high level."

Stat Line : 19 of 31 for 165 yards and a touchdown; five carries for 28 yards

The Baltimore Ravens hoped Lamar Jackson would return from injury this past weekend, but the two-time NFL MVP wasn't cleared and Tyler Huntley led the offense for the second straight week. Huntley wasn't nearly as effective facing the Browns defense as he was a week earlier against the Atlanta Falcons. Cleveland did a much better job on early downs to make life more difficult for Huntley. As a result, the Ravens struggled on third down. Baltimore converted only six of 16 opportunities. The Ravens' QB2 brings a similar skill set as Jackson. Though Huntley is far less dynamic in all areas. He can keep the offense moving, but he can't be relied upon to take the unit on his shoulders and make plays when necessary, which showed up Sunday. Even so, the Ravens were still in a position to win, but Tyler Loop missed a field goal and Derrick Henry lost a fumble in the fourth quarter, which provided the opening Cleveland needed to emerge victorious.

Stat Line : 23 of 33 for 255 yards and two touchdowns

Everyone has gotten so accustomed to Josh Allen's unbelievable feats that a day without 300 yards passing or 100 rushing yards seems mundane. Then, Allen does something extraordinary to remind everyone who he is.

During Sunday's action against the Las Vegas Raiders, Allen made a backhanded toss while being hit by a Raiders defender that went 12 yards (probably closer to 15) for a touchdown.

"It's just f—ing ridiculous, isn't it?" Bills center Connor McGovern told reporters . "I thought he was going to take off, do a little juke, get a couple yards. All the sudden, he just flicks it. I'm thinking, 'What is he doing?' But there's Keon [Coleman], just wide open. It's like playing NFL Street back in the day. Did that just happen?" Allen is the best football player on the planet right now, even if he's not producing Herculean efforts every single contest.

Score : 25-14 win vs. Philadelphia Eagles

Stat Line : 20 of 39 for 281 yards and two touchdowns

The Carolina Panthers had two weeks to prepare for a Philadelphia Eagles squad that didn't have quarterback Jalen Hurts or running back Saquon Barkley in the lineup. Carolina handled its business. Though Bryce Young didn't perform as efficiently as previously seen.

Young's 51.3 completion percentage was his worst effort this season.

However, he became only the fourth quarterback in the last 15 years to open a season with at least 280 passing yards and two touchdown passes in each of his first five games, according to Pro Football Focus . Some guys named Aaron Rodgers, Drew Brees and Peyton Manning. To take things one step further, two of those previous three were named MVP during the season they accomplished the same goal. Also, Young's 11 touchdown passes through five games is a new Panthers franchise record.

Stat Line : 30 of 36 for 305 yards and a touchdown

Caleb Williams returned from a three-week layoff due to a hamstring injury and didn't miss a beat against the Atlanta Falcons. Williams may have had finished the contest with six incomplete passes, but his performance was nearly perfect.

The third-year quarterback opened Sunday's contests with 12 straight completions. According to NFL Next Gen Stats , the Bears signal-caller completed all 24 pass attempts from a clean pocket. As ESPN's Courtney Cronin noted , Williams connected on five of six passes that traveled 10 or more air yards. Even a handful of those where he didn't connect were intentional throwaways.

"I was super juiced up to be back out here," Williams told reporters . "But I think it's just completion, completion, completion. That's the focus. That's the mindset. It's being able to keep everybody cool, calm and collected. Even myself. And other than that, it's about giving the guys a shot. Give them a good ball and let them go make plays."

Stat Line : 16 of 26 for 164 yards; eight carries for 29 yards

A pattern has developed as this season progressed. The Cleveland Browns can emerge victorious if their defense keeps them in the game and quarterback Deshaun Watson is handed the ball with an opportunity late in the contest.

Watson goes long stretches where he simply doesn't play well. For example, the Baltimore Ravens had more sacks than Browns first downs through Sunday's first three quarters.

During Cleveland's last three offensive possessions, Watson completed seven of is 10 passes attempts, including a 33-yard strike to Jerry Jeudy to place the Browns in game-winning field-goal position.

"I really don't know what to say. We got a half feeling like, 'did we even meet this week. Did we just take the week off and show up frickin' today?'" head coach Todd Monken told reporters . "...Deshaun, he knows he can play better. We can play better around him...but he's just got something in him, the ability to make a play when needed."

Score : 23-13 loss vs. Green Bay Packers

Stat Line : 34 of 54 for 258 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions

The once-potent Dallas Cowboys offense has stalled in recent weeks. Granted, the unit posted over 300 yards in back-to-back games, but the Cowboys failed to move the ball up and down the field mainly due to numerous mistakes that stall drives.

"I know I had plays out there that I want back that I know directly correlated to a turnover and us getting off the field on third down, and fourth down on one of them," Dak Prescott said Sunday after Dallas' loss to the Green Bay Packers.

"I don't have the answer for the whole team and what that is, but I believe in who we are and I know we have the talent and the men that care. We just have to put it together. Our process is right, but we have to win on Sunday."

Prescott and the entire unit can be far more effective with a little variety added to the mix.

"This season, the Cowboys now profile as dead last in the NFL in motion rate (36.5 percent), 28th out of 32 teams in under-center rate (30.4 percent) and 20th in play action rate," CBS Sports' Garrett Poddell noted .

Sean Payton's return as the Denver Broncos' offensive playcaller made the team's offense more sustainable. Though Bo Nix's continued struggles remain a significant sticking point.

Specifically, Nix is struggling with his mechanics, to work through his progressions on a regular basis and seemingly afraid to push the ball down the field. His limitations continue to stunt the Broncos offense.

"I don't know where the disconnect is right now, to be honest with you," Nix told reporters . "When the shot's called, we read it out, it's not there, you make the right play with the football and check it down and go on to the next play. I just think we're really, for some reason, struggling to find those explosive plays. That's what makes an offense really spectacular is finding explosive plays. Right now, we don't have those."

Stat Line : 23 of 41 for 276 yards, a touchdown and an interception; four carries for 12 yards and a score

Jordan Love is simultaneously playing at a high level, while in need of more help from his receivers.

Granted, Love did throw an interception that nearly turned into an pick-six during Sunday's first quarter against the Dallas Cowboys. From that point, the Green Bay Packers' signal-caller looked stellar.

Love did so while being pressured on a consistent basis. The quarterback responded with his best completion rate and yardage output of his career upon facing the highest pressure rate he's ever experienced, according to ESPN Insights .

Meanwhile, the Packers receivers have dropped more passes than any other group this season, per Pro Football Focus' Daire Carragher .

"I want to make every throw," Love told reporters . "I want these guys to make every catch. That's the expectation. Stuff happens. Drops happen. Obviously, I want those guys to make those plays, and we're capable of making those plays. But for me, it's got to be the next play mindset. You've got to move on."

Score : 34-31 win vs. Jacksonville Jaguars

Stat Line : 24 of 34 for 312 yards, three touchdowns and an interception

Quarterback play isn't about being perfect, because a perfect game doesn't exist. In a lot of cases, top quarterback play centers on an individual's reaction to adversity.

Case in point, CJ Stroud threw a costly fourth-quarter, red-zone interception Sunday when the Houston Texans had an opportunity to put away the game. Instead, the Jacksonville Jaguars responded with the game-tying field goal during the subsequent drive.

However, Stroud helped lead the Texans on a game-winning drive during their next possession. Specifically, he connected with running back Woody Marks as his checkdown option on 3rd-and-2 for 19 yards, which placed Houston in field-goal position.

"C.J.'s been hot all year. He's still hot. He's lighting it up," Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans told reporters . "He's dishing the ball around to a lot of different people. It doesn't matter who it is. Everybody who has an opportunity, they're all here. They're getting the football. He's doing an outstanding job of just leading his offense."

Stat Line : 22 of 42 for 269 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions; three carries for 30 yards

Reality has smacked the Indianapolis Colts in the face through three six weeks of play. The team is 2-4, and change is almost surely coming if a drastic turnaround doesn't happen.

Daniel Jones was the solution last year. He looked like the perfect fit for Shane Steichen's offensive scheme before a ruptured Achilles tendon ended his season. As a result, the Colts re-signed Jones this offseason.

However, this year's version of Jones has looked far more like the quarterback who eventually left the New York Giants as a first-round bust. His penchant for bad decisions and turnovers has crippled the Colts offense.

"There's some times I forced some stuff that's not there," Jones told reporters . "I gotta be smart about that. Know when it's there, when it's not and when to lay the ball off." After Indianapolis' disappointing start, everyone should start to wonder who will still be with the team a year from now.

Stat Line : 24 of 41 for 306 yards, four touchdowns and an interception

Much like his AFC South counterpart, the Jacksonville Jaguars' Trevor Lawrence produced one significant mistake Sunday. He also threw a red-zone interception. Otherwise, Lawrence did more than enough for his squad to win in London. Ultimately, Jacksonville's defense let the team down.

The Jaguars defense had been stout, particularly against the run, through the first five weeks. But Houston amassed 426 yards against Jacksonville. The Jags allowed a season-high 114 rushing yards after no team managed more than 40 during the previous stretch.

Even so, Lawrence and offense rallied from a 10-point fourth-quarter deficit to tie the game with under two minutes to play. Then, the Jaguars failed to stop CJ Stroud and Co. during Houston's final possession.

Aside from Lawrence's interception—which could have been a touchdown two plays earlier if not for a suspect holding call on a Bhaysul Tuten run—Jacksonville showed tremendous improvement in the red zone by converting its next three trips.

Score : 22-6 win vs. Los Angeles Chargers

Stat Line : 23 of 30 for 272 yards and interception

Patrick Mahomes is living his best life. The Kansas City Chiefs are undefeated and the quarterback no longer has to be Superman on a weekly basis. Instead, Mahomes now enjoys the luxury of turning around and handing the ball to the league's leading rusher, Kenneth Walker III.

"Obviously, having (No.) 9," Mahomes said of Walker's presence in the lineup, "it makes a difference both throwing and running." The Chiefs quarterback can still make all of the throws, though is creativeness has been on display less this season. When Mahomes tried to make a back-foot red-zone throw against the Los Angeles Chargers, he lobbed an awful interception. At that point, the game was still within reach. The quarterback responded during Kansas City's following possession with three completions before Walked scored.

Stat Line : 23 of 41 for 313 yards, two touchdowns and an interception

Kirk Cousins is doing everything in his power to keep the Las Vegas Raiders competitive. The team may have lost three straight after a 3-0 start, but those losses came at the hands of the Kansas City Chiefs, New England Patriots and Buffalo Bills. Only one of those outings got out of hand.

During Sunday's matchup with the Bills, Cousins threw multiple tight window lasers and the Raiders remained within striking distance until the very end.

However, Cousins also threw an ill-advised pass into double-coverage over the middle of the field, which allowed Bills linebacker Dorian Williams to snag an interception.

"It's one of these games where it's hard to sleep afterwards when you kind of think through the plays that you could have should have made," Cousins told reporters . "In a tight game like that, it comes back to haunt you."

Score : 22-6 loss vs. Kansas City Chiefs

Stat Line : 22 of 37 for 204 yards and an interception; five carries for 26 yards

Things aren't getting better for the Justin Herbert and his Los Angeles Chargers.

The team is now 0-6 and Herbert has gone six straight games without completing at least 65 percent of his passes or throwing for at least 230 yards. He's also thrown at least one interception in every single contest.

Last season, this same quarterback produced 11 games with a 65 completion percentage or better, eight outings with over 230 passing yards and six interception-less performances.

To be fair, Herbert continues to be pressured at a high rate. As Tyler Schoon of the Guilty as Charged Podcast noted, defenses have pressured Herbert on nearly 58 percent of his play-action dropback attempts.

The unfortunate part about this particular situation is no one within the organization has any clue how to fix the problems.

"I don't know," Herbert told reporters . "If I had the answers, then we'd definitely be having a different conversation."

Score : 18-16 loss vs. Arizona Cardinals

Stat Line : 25 of 33 for 222 yards and two touchdowns

Either the Los Angeles Rams bought into the hype or they're just not a good football team. According to head coach Sean McVay, it's the latter.

"We won't win a game until we figure out how to not beat ourselves," head coach Sean McVay told reporters . "So many unforced errors. So many things that are not in alignment with what we want to do, specifically on the offensive side of the ball."

When an offensive unit is struggling, the finger tends to be pointed at the quarterback, especially if that signal-caller in question is the NFL's reigning MVP. Matthew Stafford hasn't been anywhere near as sharp this season compared to last. He wasn't as aggressive Sunday as normally expected, either. In fact, his 4.8 air yards per attempt were his third-lowest average since joining the Rams five years ago, according to ESPN's Benjamin Solak .

Stat Line : 18 of 32 for 235 yards and three touchdowns; four carries for 24 yards

Drake Maye's inability to connect regularly with star wide receiver AJ Brown serves as a microcosm for this season. Maye targeted Brown 10 times Sunday but connected on only three of them.

"I'm looking forward to just growing, just building the connection," Maye told reporters . "I think there's some me, there's some plays obviously he wishes he had back. But I was just telling them in the locker room, you ain't gotta worry about No. 1. ... I told him I'm gonna keep coming his way." This season has been all about growth and reacting to adversity. Maye's performance went from playing outright awful to outstanding in a matter of a month. The quarterback and his surrounding cast still aren't clicking on all cylinders, but the entire group is clearly ascending based on recent performances.

Stat Line : 16 of 30 for 144 yards and three touchdowns; five carries for 32 yards and a score

Opportunistic may be the best way to describe Tyler Shough's performance during Sunday's victory over the New York Giants. The second-year quarterback completed 53.3 percent of his passes and threw for 144 yards. The New Orleans Saints punted on its first three offensive possessions and converted only four of 15 third-down attempts. Though 17 points came directly from turnovers. The two touchdowns were courtesy of drives starting inside the Giants' 30-yard line.

"We still have yet to put a complete game together," Shough said during a postgame interview with FOX Sports' Kristina Pink . "We got to show that. We had an opportunity [Sunday]. We're going to do it [eventually]."

New York Giants: Jameis Winston & JJ McCarthy

Score : 34-27 loss vs. New Orleans Saints

Stat Line : Winston, 14 of 26 for 152 yards, a touchdown and two interceptions; McCarthy, 11 of 21 for 243 yards, a touchdown, an interception, two carries for 26 yards

The volatility found within Jameis Winston proved too much for New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh. Harbaugh chose to bench Winston after his second interception. Enter JJ McCarthy, who joined the team three weeks ago after a trade with the Minnesota Vikings.

McCarthy provided a spark. After the third-year quarterback threw his own interception, he then rallied the Giants to 17 unanswered points and a chance to tie the game during New York's final possession.

Harbaugh must now make a decision whether McCarthy will move forward as the starting quarterback until Jaxson Dart is healthy enough to return. The 23-year-old signal-caller provides more upside and expands the Giants' offense.

"I feel like whenever you have a dual-threat quarterback that teams kind of know that it can be in the offense with him running the ball more, maybe it does kind of change their defensive mindset of how they call the game and how the defense plays," fullback Patrick Ricard told reporters . "I played with Lamar and Tyler Huntley, and that's definitely true that teams definitely have to play a running quarterback very differently. So ... we'll see what happens."

Score : 26-19 loss vs. New England Patriots

Stat Line : 20 of 30 for 252 yards, a touchdown and an interception

Geno Smith is the veteran voice of the New York Jets' offense. His standing simply isn't about being the team's starting quarterback. The roster also leans on his experience due to the youth found around him.

"I think we're a very young offense... a lot of guys have been making plays and stepping up," Smith said when asked about New York's offensive inconsistencies. "Getting some guys back and getting healthy again is really going to help us a lot." To the quarterback's point, the team's leading rusher Sunday, as well as its top and third-leading receivers, are all 22 years old. The Jets' starting offensive tackles and first-round tight end all are all 23 or younger. It falls on Smith to get these individuals up to speed and make them competitive. Smith is doing a decent job in his role, but he personally hasn't been consistent enough.

Score : 25-14 loss vs. Carolina Panthers

Stat Line : 26 of 45 for 215 yards and a touchdown

Jalen Hurts' surprise trip to injured reserve due to a blood clot in his calf led to Tanner McKee starting Sunday for the Philadelphia Eagles. The Eagles already had their issues on offense and a transition at quarterback only magnified those problems.

The McKee-led unit managed 222 yards and finished six of 16 during third and fourth downs. The Eagles were one-dimensional and predictable. McKee is better working from shotgun. He also didn't have much help from a run game or playaction passing attack, because Saquon Barkley and Will Shipley didn't play. Furthermore, Carson Steele suffered an injury. Dameon Pierce managed only 35 yards on 12 carries.

McKee could have played better. At the same time, the entire Eagles offense is banged up and not performing well.

"We've got to be able to score more points, period," head coach Nick Sirianni told reporters . "It's on everybody, right? … It's not just one coach on an island. It's not just one player on the island. It's not just one side of the ball that's on an island. It's the ultimate team game. We all have to do better, period."

Score : 26-19 win vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Stat Line : 33 of 49 for 253 yards, two touchdowns and an interception

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers bombarded Aaron Rodgers with pressure throughout Sunday's contest. In the end, the 42-year-old quarterback and his Pittsburgh Steelers found a way to respond and escaped overtime with a victory.

Tampa sacked Rodgers five times and collected 10 quarterback hits. The Steelers trailed 13-3 coming out of halftime. The team response in building a 4-2 record is vital from a macro perspective.

From a micro point of view, Rodgers' growing confidence in second-round rookie wide receiver Germie Bernard can be critical to how the rest of the season progresses. Bernard caught 11 passes Sunday after snagging 13 through the first five games.

"You need to ease expectations," Rogers told reporters , "but there comes a time when the confidence starts to match the potential. And I think we're reaching that time with Germie. Very proud of him. Obviously, the fourth down, probably should just catch it and back up, but he made a lot of nice plays today, a lot of smart plays, a lot of good catches."

Stat Line : 27 of 51 for 278 yards and two interceptions

Prior to Sunday's action, Sam Darnold was tied for the league lead with seven interceptions. Let's keep in mind he missed nearly two full games. He committed at least two turnovers in three of Seattle last four outings.

"I think it's BS for me to keep turning the ball over," Darnold said after Thursday's loss. "It's not fair to our defense. It's not fair to our special teams group. Not fair, really, to the entire team."

To make matter's worse, Darnold's latest turnovers came during the fourth quarter and overtime. The second was particularly egregious, because the veteran signal-caller never recognized the deep defender, who easily undercut a hole-shot along the sideline for the interception. Four plays later, the Broncos kicked the game-winning field goal.

Score : 26-19 loss vs. Pittsburgh Steelers

Stat Line : 22 of 43 for 164 yards, a touchdown and two interceptions; four carries for 39 yards

Jalon Daniels is a great story and the type of professional football player everyone wants to see succeed because he's the quintessential underdog story.

"He has like this aura about him," wide receiver Chris Godwin told reporters last week. "He comes in; he's very charismatic. He's got like this childlike enthusiasm that he plays the game with. And it's dope to see. Guys like that, they keep you young, man. It's like when he's out there, he's the star of his own movie." However, the NFL is a bottom-line business. Daniels didn't get the job done Sunday against the Pittsburgh Steelers. His inexperience combined with skill-set limitations cap what the undrafted rookie can do when leading an offense. Daniels does have some playmaking traits, especially as a runner, but he threw for fewer than 190 yards in three straight appearances. During this past weekend's outing, his completion percentage also dropped to 51.2 percent.

Score : 26-20 win vs. Indianapolis Colts

Stat Line : 11 of 22 for 102 yards, a touchdown and an interception

Cam Ward should be happy the Tennessee Titans' defense and special teams played well Sunday, because those efforts will take pressure off the quarterback despite another questionable outing. The Titans are finally in the win column despite Tennessee's offense manufacturing fewer than 190 yards. Ward completed 50 percent of his passes and threw for season-low 102 yards. The Colts were able to key on the second-year quarterback's eyes, knocked down four passes at the line of scrimmage and intercepted another. Indianapolis' own implosion led to the loss more than anything Ward contributed. A win is a win in the NFL. The Titans can't complain after their first victory. But a glaring issue still remains at the game's most important position. The Cleveland Browns will field a much better and more aggressive defense next weekend than the one Ward faced Sunday.

articles.title: After Chris Ballard's firing, Colts find themselves staring at a major overhaul
articles.summary: The Colts could be facing major changes
articles.body:
Even if you question what good firing a general manager during the season does, it wasn't a major surprise when the Indianapolis Colts fired GM Chris Ballard on Monday.

The Colts have made the playoffs once since 2018 and have no playoff wins since then. Their best record since 2021 is 9-8, and they've gone 8-9 in each of the two seasons. This season they sit at 2-4, with a loss to the previously winless Titans on Sunday and victories over one- and two-win teams.

Ballard's biggest problem was getting the quarterback spot right. When he arrived, Andrew Luck was in place, and his sudden retirement set the franchise back. But Ballard has had the better part of a decade to get this position right, and it just hasn't happened.

Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Basketball league for the 2026-27 NBA season

The Colts might have thought they had their guy in Daniel Jones a year ago when the Colts started 8-2 and appeared to be a playoff squad. That's when they traded for cornerback Sauce Gardner — a move that blew up in their faces.

Carlie Irsay-Gordon has been taking a hands-on approach to ownership of the club since her father's passing, even donning headsets during games to get a better feel how the organization runs, top to bottom. It would not be hard to imagine that more significant changes will follow eventually.

"​Making this change during the season was a deliberate decision," Irsay-Gordon said in her statement. "Waiting would only delay the important work that needs to begin now. We will conduct a thorough search for our next general manager and take the time necessary to identify the right leader for the future of this organization."

Does this mean changes to the coaching staff will follow? A trade-deadline purge? A new quarterback next offseason? Let's break down what's next for the Colts during this transition period.

Trade deadline looms, and the Colts should be sellers

Let's first be transparent: Irsay-Gordon also said the Colts plan to be competitive.

"I also want to be clear: this decision does not change our goals for the season. We have a lot of football in front of us, and I expect us to compete, improve, and win football games," Irsay-Gordon's statement also said.

That's a noble intention, but there's also a cold reality. They're 2-4 and likely need to look vastly better over the next few weeks to avoid the inevitable.

The big picture is that the Gardner trade, which sapped the Colts of their 2026 and 2027 first-round picks, has significantly damaged their offseason draft-pick lot. What stings a little extra is that the 2027 NFL Draft appears to be one of the more top-heavy classes in the past few years, and the Colts are currently tied for the sixth-worst record in the league. Wherever they wind up, the Jets will enjoy that windfall.

The Colts have to consider moving on from some of their more valuable pieces as a way of helping recoup some of the lost value. Irsay-Gordon expressed a desire to expeditiously move on from Ballard, and she should endorse similar aggression when it comes to moving assets, starting with prior to the trade deadline in the coming weeks.

One obvious one would be defensive tackle DeForest Buckner, who is 32 years old and headed for free agency in the spring. There likely would be multiple teams interested in his services. Grover Stewart is 33 and in the same position. Either or both could be available.

Other pieces to consider moving: wide receiver Josh Downs and safety Cam Bynum. Both are younger pieces who could fetch decent value if moved.

But what about Jonathan Taylor? From a value perspective, it would make sense to unload a pricy running back with an injury history and arguably at his peak (or moving past it) with nearly 2,000 career touches.

There also could be a conversation about moving offensive guard Quenton Nelson, who is also in a free-agent season. The question is whether Irsay-Gordon has the same sentimentality as her father, Jim Irsay, who was known to be fond of both Taylor and Nelson and likely viewed them as career-long Colts.

In-season general manager firings tend to be more rare, but when they happen, it can be an indication of a fire sale to come. This played out in Miami after GM Chris Grier was fired during the regular season a year ago. Jaelen Phillips was dealt, and the Dolphins dangled Jaylen Waddle and Bradley Chubb, eventually trading Waddle in the offseason.

Barring a quick Colts turnaround, it would be hard to imagine they're not open for business, and they have plenty of options to move.

Quarterback future looking dim, with limited options

The Colts' move to re-sign Jones last offseason isn't standing the test of time. Jones was off to a career-best flourish to start last season, but he hit a wall when injuries mounted, eventually missing the rest of the season with a ruptured Achilles tendon.

Jones' quick return from the injury suffered in December should be viewed as a strong commitment to his rehab and professionalism, but the product he's put out there this season hasn't been a match in excellence. Jones ranks near the bottom among most qualified passers. He's had interceptions in every game but one (and two in the loss to the Titans on Sunday) and is on pace for his worst career completion percentage (59.6).

Remember, too, that the Colts allowed Michael Pittman Jr. to walk, knowing they couldn't keep him, Jones and Alec Pierce. Right now, Pierce is on IR, with five catches in two games so far this season.

One way or another, the Colts are more likely to move on from Jones this offseason. Sure, he still has time to turn things around, but counting on that feels awfully risky.

We know Anthony Richardson's story, and he doesn't realistically figure to be among the potential solutions, either. Richardson had his chances to claim the Colts' starting job, and his failures were a big strike against Ballard.

The next general manager is going to have to figure out how best to acquire a quarterback this offseason and make it work without a first-round pick.

Even if there are reasonably interesting QB prospects who linger long enough to be available in Round 2 of the draft, the most prudent and likely option would be a veteran who outplayed his welcome elsewhere, perhaps similar to Kyler Murray, Kirk Cousins or Tua Tagovailoa — a bridge option until they find something better.

There will be options, but the quality of those options will be far below "unquestioned franchise starter." This is just another indication of the breadth of the Colts' rebuild, especially if they sell off pieces at the deadline.

articles.title: Sauce Gardner Injured, Latest Rumors on Colts Star's Timeline to Return from Calf Injury
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts are having an eventful Monday.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts are having an eventful Monday.

On the same day that general manager Chris Ballard was fired , star cornerback Sauce Gardner reportedly was diagnosed with a mild calf strain and is "week-to-week," per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport .

According to Rapoport, "Gardner is expected to miss some time, but not an extended period."

Gardner, 25, is a two-time Pro Bowler and two-time first-team All-Pro selection. This season he's appeared in all six games for the Colts, registering 17 tackles and four passes defensed. While he isn't having a signature season, being without him will make the Colts demonstrably worse against the pass.

The Colts paid a hefty price to bring him aboard last season, trading two first-round picks (2026-27) and wideout Adonai Mitchell to the New York Jets. It was expected to be the sort of move that took the Colts over the top as contenders.

It hasn't quite worked that way. At the time of the deal last season, the Colts were 7-2. Since the trade, the team has gone just 3-11.

That's not on Gardner, of course. Last season's schedule got far more difficult down the stretch, Daniel Jones was lost for the season last year—prompting the team to lure Philip Rivers out of retirement—and there are now major questions about the team's coaching staff and front office.

But Sunday's loss against the previously winless Tennessee Titans was a new low.

That earned the team plenty of boos from their home fans. Not that the Colts blamed them.

"I'm pissed off, too," veteran defensive lineman DeForest Buckner told reporters . "I'm sick and tired of the same song and dance every year."

The steps aren't going to get any easier without Gardner.

articles.title: 'Self-Inflicted… S--t,' Justin Herbert, Jim Harbaugh, McDaniel's Chargers Called Out by NFL Coach
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers and first-year offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel drew a stern rebuke from opposing coaches as their losing streak stretched to six games to open the 2026 NFL season.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers and first-year offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel drew a stern rebuke from opposing coaches as their losing streak stretched to six games to open the 2026 NFL season.

The Athletic's Mike Sando reported the coaches believe McDaniel "installed the graduate-level version of his offense with all its shifts, motions and formations from Week 1."

"There are a lot of formations and motions that he's gonna present to you," they told Sando. "I don't know if that's easy to operate for those guys or not. And then it's like an unquantifiable ripple effect — then they start having self-inflicted penalties and s--t like that."

The Chargers mustered just 259 yards of offense in Sunday's 22-6 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. Along with committing two turnovers, they were flagged seven times for 59 yards.

The result wasn't necessarily surprising since it was more of the same from Los Angeles. Still, you keep thinking something might click with the offense at some point given the combined presence of McDaniel, coach John Harbaugh and quarterback Justin Herbert.

McDaniel was the architect of some strong units in his one year as offensive coordinator with the San Francisco 49ers and then coach of the Miami Dolphins. Herbert is arguably a better pure thrower than what he had in San Francisco and Miami as well.

One coach questioned whether this is simply a bad combo of QB and scheme.

"In Miami, when they were rolling, it was because of the explosive skill they had, and a phenomenal system," they said to Sando. "San Francisco rolls because of Brock Purdy. I just don't know if Herbert can handle that system. That is my take, and then couple that with their line being the worst we've seen."

In what's a common refrain for his NFL career, injuries to the offensive line aren't making Herbert's life easier in the pocket. That consideration doesn't fully explain why he's averaging 190.2 passing yards per game while ranking last in QBR (29.9) with a league-high eight interceptions.

Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio reported there's a "growing buzz" that Harbaugh will dismiss McDaniel "soon." If that happens, passing game coordinator Adam Gase would likely run the offense.

Los Angeles has a bye in Week 7, so this would be a good time to make a big move to the coaching staff if Harbaugh has any serious reservations.

articles.title: Jim Harbaugh Involved In Wild Stat As Chargers Start 0-6 for 1st Time Since 2000 NFL Season
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers fell to 0-6 for the first time since 2000, but for head coach Jim Harbaugh, it's a familiar feeling.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers fell to 0-6 for the first time since 2000, but for head coach Jim Harbaugh, it's a familiar feeling.

That's because Harbaugh was one of three quarterbacks to start for the Chargers during the 2000 campaign , in which the team went 0-11 before finishing with a 1-15 record.

Harbaugh played in seven games for the Chargers and produced 1,416 yards, eight touchdowns and 10 interceptions. His final career game came in a Week 11 relief appearance for Ryan Leaf.

The 2026 Chargers haven't fared any better, suffering their most disappointing loss of the year in Sunday's 22-6 laugher against the Kansas City Chiefs.

Harbaugh will try to get the Chargers back on track during their bye week before they return to face the Los Angeles Rams on Nov. 1.

articles.title: B/R Experts Week 7 NFL Power Rankings
articles.summary: If the NFL has taught us anything, it's that we know nothing. It's a lesson we learn again each and every week.
articles.body:
If the NFL has taught us anything, it's that we know nothing. It's a lesson we learn again each and every week.

Six weeks into the 2026 campaign, the reigning Super Bowl champions are sitting at .500 after back-to-back losses. The preseason Super Bowl favorite is 2-4 after losing at home to a tomato can. Of the three teams to make it to 5-0, just one had a winning record a year ago. One playoff team from 2025 has yet to win a game.

Every team in both the AFC North and NFC North has a winning record after six weeks. Just two teams in the AFC South and NFC South combined do.

It's enough to make your head spin—and we're only a third of the way into the regular season.

Bleacher Report NFL analysts Gary Davenport , Kris Knox , Maurice Moton and Brent Sobleski have taken their Dramamine and are diving into the madness once more to separate contenders from pretenders and rank all 32 teams from worst to first.

ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN | CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND | JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN | NE | NYG | NO | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SEA | SF | TB | TEN | WAS

The Miami Dolphins had a Week 6 bye, and we didn't change their ranking. On an encouraging note, the Dolphins battled the Minnesota Vikings and Cincinnati Bengals in one-score games, a step up from their double-digit blowout losses in Weeks 1-3.

In Week 7, Miami may field its young core of rookie receivers if Caleb Douglas has recovered from an ankle injury. Along with Chris Bell and Kevin Coleman Jr., he could be the future of the Dolphins' pass-catching group. -- Moton

The Los Angeles Chargers entered 2026 with high expectations after back-to-back 11-win seasons. They head into the bye week one of two remaining teams in the league who have yet to win a game.

Simply put, the Chargers aren't doing anything well. Los Angeles ran the ball 22 times Sunday—for 73 yards. Justin Herbert barely cracked 200 passing yards and hsn't thrown multiple touchdown passes in a game yet this season. The offensive line is in shambles. No team in the league has turned the ball over more.

While addressing the media after the game, head coach Jim Harbaugh said changes are coming over the bye week.

"Definitely, offensively, we need to evaluate," he said. We need to look at it all — everything we're doing, how we're doing it."

I home embattled offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is renting. -- Davenport

Week 6 Result: Won at Indianapolis 26-20

The Tennessee Titans picked up their first win of the season on Sunday by taking advantage of the Indianapolis Colts' mistakes. However, Tennessee doesn't look like a team that is going to string together wins any time soon.

The Titans' next three games will come against teams that currently have a winning record.

It's just hard to pinpoint any one thing that the Titans do well. Cam Ward continues to underwhelm as an NFL starter, and he completed just 50 percent of his passes for 102 yards against a bad Colts defense. While Tennessee's defense has shown flashes of promise at times this season, it gave up 399 yards in Indy and isn't the sort of unit that will regularly take over games.

Tennessee will certainly welcome Sunday's victory, but it does little to suggest that Ward and head coach Robert Saleh are long-term answers for this franchise. -- Knox

Week 6 Result: Lost vs. Pittsburgh 26-19 (OT)

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers played decent football with undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels under center, but they need Baker Mayfield back from a dislocated thumb to stack wins. According to NFL insider James Palmer , Tampa Bay may get him back for a critical NFC South showdown against the Carolina Panthers this week.

With one win against the sputtering Dallas Cowboys, the Buccaneers sit near the bottom of the power rankings, but Mayfield could help them move up with upcoming games against the Panthers and the Atlanta Falcons. -- Moton

There's good news and bad news for the Washington Commanders.

The good news ahead of Monday night's road tilt is that even at 1-3-1, the team is still in the race in the NFC East. Every other team in the division lost in Week 6. The "leader" sits at 3-2-1. Win the game, and despite a slow start and another Jayden Daniels injury the Commanders would be in the mix in the division.

The bad news is that road trip is to San Francisco to face arguably the NFL's best team. A loss sends the team into the basement of the NFL's worst division.

And the 2026 season will be perilously close to coming off the rails. -- Sobleski

The Tennessee Titans looked like one of the two worst teams in the NFL through the first five weeks of 2026. Somehow, the Indianapolis Colts were worse on Sunday.

Indy blew a 13-0 halftime lead and a legitimate shot to get to .500 against the previously winless Titans.

The Colts team we saw start 8-2 last season is a thing of the past, and it isn't coming back in 2026, if ever. Indy's defense, which came into Week 6 ranked 28th overall, continues to be a liability, and quarterback Daniel Jones is starting to become one.

Jones threw a pair of interceptions in scoring position against the Titans while completing just 22 of 42 pass attempts. Six weeks into the season, he looks less like the budding star we saw in 2025 and a lot more like the inconsistent quarterback the New York Giants gave up on two years ago. Injuries in the receiving corps certainly haven't helped, but Jones isn't even playing the game-manager role well enough.

The Colts are spiraling, and things could get worse with road games against the Minnesota Vikings and Jacksonville Jaguars on deck. -- Knox

Week 6 Result: Won at Los Angeles Rams 18-16

The Arizona Cardinals have looked like one of the league's worst teams over the past few weeks, but they stopped their four-game skid with an unexpected road win over the Los Angeles Rams.

The fact that Arizona pulled off the upset without star rookie running back Jeremiyah Love and after trading away wideout Marvin Harrison Jr. should catch the attention of future opponents. The Cardinals might not be a great team overall, but they have a collection of offensive skill players that can at least keep games interesting.

On Sunday, the offense was effective enough to retake the lead after Arizona lost it with just 47 seconds in regulation.

Are the Cardinals playoff contenders? Probably not, but the Rams may not be the last opponents they upset this season, either. -- Knox

Week 6 Result: Lost at New England 26-19

Aside from a 23-12 loss to the Chicago Bears in Week 4, the New York Jets have been competitive, but they're still not good enough to beat perennial playoff contenders. Gang Green's best win is against the AFC North-leading Cleveland Browns, a young team on the rise.

Rookie first-rounders Kenyon Sadiq and Omar Cooper Jr. have had their breakout games. Now, they need to establish consistency to be key week-to-week contributors in the Jets offense. -- Moton

Week 6 Result: Won at New York Giants 34-27

The New Orleans Saints came close to putting together a statement game, but the New York Giants turned it into a fourth-quarter nail-biter. Saints fans shouldn't let head coach Kellen Moore off the hook yet. Keep him on the hot seat until the team plays complete games from start to finish.

Tyler Shough didn't take any sacks against the Giants, which is ideal for a quarterback playing with two broken bones in his non-throwing hand (h/t ESPN's Adam Schefter ). New Orleans can gain some momentum with a win over the Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris. If they pull that off, Moore would quiet his critics for now. -- Moton

Every NFL team is dealing with injuries. Though no squad has been bitten by the injury bug worse than the Philadelphia Eagles. The team placed quarterback Jalen Hurts on injured reserve last week due to a blood clot in his calf. Philadelphia was down to its fourth running back Sunday against the Carolina Panthers. Wide receiver DeVonta Smith has been banged up this season. The list continues, but a team down or hobbled at quarterback, running back and wide receiver is a tough enough starting point.

To make matters worse, Philadelphia's next three games are all against NFC East rivals. The Eagles' season could realistically be out of hand before the team even reaches its bye--especially with Hurts now done for the year. -- Sobleski
