It was bad enough when the Dallas Cowboys' defense wasn't working. Now, the same can be said about the squad's previously potent offense.

Against the Green Bay Packers, Dallas produced one explosive play in the passing game and none within the run game. Considering how much talent is found on that side of the ball, that level of performance is unacceptable, particularly when Dallas needs to play well offensively each week to counteract the team's defensive struggles. It's the second straight week an opponent held Dallas to 16 or fewer points after scoring 30 or more in three straight. Fortunately, the schedule turns in Dallas' favor. The Philadelphia Eagles will still be without quarterback Jalen Hurts next Monday. The Arizona Cardinals and Indianapolis Colts follow and they both own losing records. Considering the state of the NFC East, the Cowboys aren't out of the mix even with their performance as of late. -- Sobleski

The Atlanta Falcons are coming off consecutive losses, though the good news is they showed the ability to play through a poor start with their passing game. Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson Jr. are the key playmakers for a run-first offense, but Michael Penix Jr. leads a respectable aerial attack.

If Penix stays healthy, Atlanta can overcome an 2-4 start. He elevates his pass-catching group, specifically wideout Drake London and tight end Kyle Pitts Sr. in a balanced offense. -- Moton

Week 6 Result: Lost vs. New Orleans 34-27

Head coach John Harbaugh finally had enough of the "Jameis Winston experience" and benched the New York Giants QB2 in favor of JJ McCarthy, whom the team acquired three weeks ago.

Truthfully, this outcome was expected. Winston has always lived by Bruce Arians' "No risk it, no biscuit" mantra. The 2015 No. 1 overall draft pick can sling the ball all over the yard, but it's only a matter of time before he makes a critical mistake and throws it to someone wearing the wrong jersey. McCarthy should be viewed differently, because his game brings the Giants closer to what Jaxson Dart could do. Granted, Dart's return to the lineup remains highly anticipated. Until then, McCarthy deserves a chance to see what he can do since the team knows exactly what it'll get from Winston on a week-to-week basis. -- Sobleski

Week 6 Result: Won vs. Jacksonville 34-31 (London)

The Houston Texans didn't get their first win of 2026 until Week 5. They've now won two in a row and have reentered the AFC South picture with a victory over the rival Jacksonville Jaguars.

Houston's defense hasn't been nearly as dominant as it was a year ago. However, C.J. Stroud is playing at a Pro Bowl level and leads a balanced offense—when healthy—that will give the Texans a chance to win more often than not.

New wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. had just three receptions for 34 yards in his Texans debut on Sunday, but he should help open up the passing attack.

Climbing out of a2-4 hole will be difficult, of course. However, Houston did exactly that last season and made it to the divisional round. This is a team that must be taken seriously moving forward, even if it is still chasing the early playoff field. -- Knox

Here's how most people expected this season to go for the Raiders. Kirk Cousins would open the season as the starter under center, but as the losses mounted the reigns in the offense would be handed to rookie No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza.

Well, the Raiders have indeed dropped three straight. But don't hold your breath waiting for Mendoza to get the keys. You'll turn blue.

For the second time in three weeks, the Raiders gave an AFC heavyweight all they could handle in Week 6. Cousins was a big reason why, lighting up the Bills for 313 passing yards.

It's going to come down to the Raiders' priorities. Once the team's unlikely postseason hopes have been dashed, then odds are we'll see Mendoza take over.

But given how feisty these Raiders have been to date, those playoff aspirations may be around a while longer than we thought. -- Davenport

Rumors of the Los Angeles Rams being an unstoppable force were greatly exaggerated.

After rolling into the regular season with massive expectations, the Rams are 2-4 and sitting in the NFC West basement. It doesn't feel like their rough start to the season has been fluky, either.

The eventual return of Myles Garrett may not be enough to fix a leaky defense, and it will do nothing to address L.A.'s disastrous special-teams unit. While Matthew Stafford and the offense have been enough to keep the Rams in games more often than not, they could have a tough time doing that if Davante Adams' apparent non-contact injury proves to be significant.

Teams don't usually face must-win games in October, but next week's trip to Las Vegas could bring exactly that for the Rams. -- Knox

The Detroit Lions are one of the most Jekyll-and-Hyde teams in the league.

The offense has been lethally efficient—led by quarterback Jared Goff, running back Jahmyr Gibbs and wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown, Detroit is sixth in the league in total offense and leads the NFC at 32.8 points per game. You know that the Lions are going to score.

Unfortunately, you also know the Lions can't stop anyone from scoring. The Lions have been atrocious defensively—especially against the pass. Detroit entered Week 6 as the only team in the league allowing 400 yards of offense per game. The Lions are also dead last against the pass and have allowed just under 30 points per contest.

Given those defensive deficiencies, it's kind of difficult to imagine these Lions making a deep playoff run. Winning (or losing) shootouts every week will only get you so far. -- Davenport

Week 6 Result: Won at Tampa Bay 26-19 (OT)

The Pittsburgh Steelers overcame a 13-point fourth-quarter deficit to capture a victory in overtime against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. With each passing week, the Steelers discover more about their team.

Previously, Pittsburgh realized its offense needed to run through running back Jaylen Warren. During Sunday's action, rookie wide receiver Germie Bernard emerged as a legitimate threat. Bernard caught 11 passes for 83 yards and a touchdown after coming into the contest with only 13 receptions. Veterans bespeckle the Steelers lineup. This team is experienced enough to compete with any team on a weekly basis. Pittsburgh's lineup is far from perfect, but the coaching staff and its players continue to work through adversity, having won three of their last four games. -- Sobleski

Everyone understands the Cincinnati Bengals are built around quarterback Joe Burrow and wide receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Technically, the Bengals don't need a balanced offense when they can throw the ball all over the yard. But it would be beneficial if the squad could run the ball more effectively.

Coming out of their bye, the Bengals are counted among the league's bottom five rushing offenses. Last season, Chase Brown posted his first 1,000-yard campaign. He hasn't been nearly as effective this fall, averaging a career-low 3.5 yards per carry.

With the extra time to prepare for the Baltimore Ravens, Cincinnati should have placed an emphasis on getting its running game where it needs to be so the Bengals offense can become even more dangerous. -- Sobleski

The Cleveland Browns have developed a formula, leading to the team's unexpected yet AFC North-leading 4-2 record. Really, it's rather simple. Cleveland needs to play top-notch defense for three-plus quarters before the team can hand the ball to Deshaun Watson and let the quarterback create a play when it's absolutely needed.

Watson hasn't played particularly well this season. However, he's done enough, specifically in crunch time, to help his team establish a winning record. Despite the early success, this approach doesn't seem sustainable when the Browns eventually face the better teams. For example, Lamar Jackson wasn't in the Baltimore Ravens' lineup during Sunday's matchup. Fortunately, Cleveland's remaining docket looks rather manageable. In fact, the Browns face only one team with a winning record between now and the start of December. -- Sobleski

The Green Bay Packers appear to be figuring out who they are.

The Packers haven't run the ball well at all this year, and that continued Sunday night against the Dallas Cowboys—26 carries for 57 yards is…less than ideal. But for the second straight week the Pack carved up a defense with vertical passes. The score would have been that much more lopsided had their not been multiple drops, and quarterback Jordan Love told reporters the team has things to clean up moving forward.

"I want to make every throw," Love said. "I want these guys to make every catch. That's the expectation. Stuff happens. Drops happen. Obviously, I want those guys to make those plays, and we're capable of making those plays. But for me, it's got to be the next play mindset. You've got to move on."

The Packers need to smooth the rough edges quickly—Green Bay's next four opponents are all over .500. -- Davenport

Week 6 Result: Won at Philadelphia 25-14

The Carolina Panthers are the best team in the NFC South a third of the way through the regular season. Many won't praise them for beating the Philadelphia Eagles, who were without starting quarterback Jalen Hurts and star running back Saquan Barkley and fielded a reshuffled offensive line, though Carolina has been without its starting cornerbacks, Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson, due to injuries.

The Panthers are proving last year's NFC South title wasn't a fluke. Bryce Young is playing his best football, with 11 touchdown passes and just two interceptions. They're a legitimate playoff team this year and are slowly climbing in our power rankings. -- Moton

The Baltimore Ravens whiffed on a major opportunity to take control of the AFC North after six weeks of play. Instead, they fell to 4-2 and third place.

Cleveland couldn't do anything Sunday through the first three quarters of play. In fact, the Ravens generated more sacks than the Browns had first downs at that point. But a missed field goal by kicker Tyler Loop and a lost fumble by running back Derrick Henry during Baltimore's initial fourth-quarter possessions opened the door and Cleveland took advantage. The Ravens hoped they could win two in a row without Lamar Jackson in the lineup. They failed to do so. Realistically, this same squad will be far better once Jackson is healthy and back on the field. -- Sobleski

It's probably not fair to say that the Seattle Seahawks are suffering from a Super Bowl hangover. Rather, the defending champs are sitting at 3-3 because of two key issues.

Backfield injuries have prevented the Seahawks from running the ball effectively. As a team, Seattle has averaged just 3.9 yards per carry. This has allowed opposing defenses to focus on pressuring quarterback Sam Darnold, who has been the team's other issue.

With seven interceptions in less than five full games, Darnold has actively cost Seattle wins.

The Seahawks are now playing catch-up in the NFC West, though they have a pretty clear path to righting the ship. If Darnold can better protect the ball, and Seattle can get Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price healthy, the Seahawks will be a tough out for anyone. -- Knox

Last week, the Chicago Bears got their doors blown off by the Packers in Green Bay. With the return of quarterback Caleb Williams to the lineup in Week 6, they returned the favor in Atlanta.

It's not reflected in the final score, but this was a game the Bears led 31-7. Williams topped 300 passing yards in the win and missed on just six of 36 passing attempts. Williams told reporters after the win that he was glad to be back out there—but he has room to improve.

"I didn't know that I went 30 for 36, and so I've got to go obviously back and watch the tape," Williams said. "I missed a couple things."

When firing on all cylinders, these Bears have a ceiling as high any time in the league. But they need to be more consistent to be considered among the league's elite. -- Davenport

Week 6 Result: Lost vs. Houston 34-31 (London)

Jaguars cornerback/receiver Travis Hunter had his breakout game as a two-way player on Sunday. The Colorado product logged an interception, four catches, 59 receiving yards, and a touchdown. It was exactly the sort of game that the Jags envisioned when they traded up to take Hunter second overall.

Unfortunately, Hunter can't cover everyone, and Jacksonville's secondary is beginning to look like a problem. The Jags came into Week 6 ranked 27th in net yards per pass attempt allowed and 30th in passing yards allowed. They surrendered another 306 passing yards against Houston on Sunday.

Jacksonville features an elite run defense and boasts an offense that can match points with anyone when Trevor Lawrence is taking care of the football. That could be enough for the Jags to control the AFC South and push into the postseason with plenty of momentum.

However, it's fair to wonder if Jacksonville can corral top signal-callers in January. -- Knox

Week 6 Result: Won vs. Seattle 17-14 (OT)

Usually, a hard-fought victory over the defending Super Bowl champions would earn a team some kudos from the crew calling the game. But after a game in which he threw for just 107 yards, Denver's Bo Nix was put on full blast by Prime Video's Ryan Fitzpatrick .

"It's almost disrespectful to the quarterback position how he's playing football right now," Fitzpatrick said. "First of all, the guy doesn't want to throw the ball. That's fine. He's throwing to the flats, he's throwing behind, but he has no trust from his coach."

He said quite a bit more, but that just about sums it up.

There's no denying that Nix isn't playing especially well. He's also not getting any help from his run game—JK Dobbins carried the ball 17 times for 41 yards Thursday night.

Denver has plenty to work on as they get ready to head south to face the Arizona Cardinals. – Davenport

Week 6 Result: Won vs. New York Jets 26-19

After two losses in the first three weeks, the New England Patriots have rattled off three consecutive wins, and Drake Maye has his swagger back. Over the last three outings, he's thrown for 10 touchdowns and just one interception, with one of those contests a win over the rival Bills.

Maye and newly acquired Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown have a lot to work on with their on-field connection, but they have time to get in sync. The duo will need to click in Thursday night's matchup against the high-scoring Chicago Bears. -- Moton

The Buffalo Bills head into their Week 7 bye with only one blemish on their record: a three-point loss to the New England Patriots. So far, they've overcompensated for a leaky defense, which ranked in the bottom five in scoring and total yards entering Week 6.

During the off week, defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard must address his unit and make some adjustments. On the other side of the Bills' bye, they could face a Lamar Jackson-led Baltimore Ravens squad and the unbeaten Minnesota Vikings. They'll need a well-rounded performance on both sides of the ball to beat those teams. -- Moton

There isn't a more surprising team in the NFL this year (at least in a positive way) than the undefeated Minnesota Vikings.

Naysayers will point to a relatively easy schedule and offensive inconsistency as reasons why the Vikings aren't as good their record. But Minnesota's ultra-aggressive defense is absolutely legit—second in yards allowed, third against the pass, fifth against the run and first in points allowed.

Edge-rusher Andrew Van Ginkel told reporters the defense's strength lies in its versatility.

"Things are constantly changing," Van Ginkel said. "It could be changing game to game. It could be changing from series to series. It could be changing from play to play. It could be changing within the play."

That defense is going to be tested coming up—after facing the hapless Colts at home in Week 7, the Vikes take on two of the league's best offenses in the Lions and Bills. -- Davenport

Week 6 Result: Won vs. Los Angeles Chargers 22-6

If the Chiefs make a deep playoff run this year (which appears more likely by the week), then the offseason acquisition of running back Kenneth Walker III may be the most impactful signing of free agency in 2026.

The addition of the MVP of Super Bowl 60 has added a new dimension to Kansas City's offense, and Walker had another big game against the Bolts Sunday—21 total touches, 139 yards and a pair of touchdowns. His 655 rushing yards for the season are the most ever over a player's first five games with a team.

In Week 6 at least, the absence of No. 1 wide receiver Rashee Rice didn't have a major impact. But Kansas City is about to hit the road to face Walker's old team in Seattle and the rival Broncos at Mile High.

Navigating that double-dip without taking loss No. 1 of the season short-handed won't be easy. But it's safe to say that if Kansas City ever left, it's back. -- Davenport

Through five-plus weeks, the San Francisco 49ers have looked like the best team in football. That's unlikely to change on Monday night against the Washington Commanders.

San Francisco's defense has been playoff-caliber, its offense features a top-10 rushing attack, and Brock Purdy is playing at an MVP level. The big question is whether mounting injuries will eventually become too much, as was the case last season.

Deebo Samuel was the latest key contributor to go down, and he's expected to miss multiple weeks with a hamstring injury. It'll be interesting to see how Kyle Shanahan and the offense adjust against Washington. -- Knox

articles.title: Washington Commanders face unbeaten San Francisco 49ers in Monday night football showdown
articles.summary: The undefeated San Francisco 49ers host the struggling Washington Commanders on Monday, with Purdy's passing attack facing a bottom-tier pass defense.
articles.body: This was a wild weekend of football. Most of the chaos started with college football, but some of it carried over into the NFL. I wouldn't say we had the same level of upsets or anything, but there are some interesting things going on in the league. The Browns are the leader in their division, which seems like the first time in years. The Colts fell apart and gave the Titans their first win. The Falcons made a game of it late, but the Bears prevailed and showed how good they can be with Caleb Williams under center. The Cardinals beat the Rams at home. The Chargers are potentially the worst team in football. The phrase "Any Given Sunday" rings true this year more than any other time I can remember. Could it happen on Monday with the Commanders and 49ers playing? The Washington Commanders come into the game with a 1-3-1 record. It has been an interesting season for the Commanders, who have suffered injuries, bad play, and poor clock management throughout the season. They started the season with the Eagles, and although the final score of the game was close, the actual game wasn't exactly impressive for Washington. They scored a late touchdown to give themselves a chance, but the Eagles were in control for most of the game. The next week, they played Dallas and were blown out. They lost their starting quarterback in the process. In Week 3, they hosted the defending champion Seahawks and narrowly defeated them 33-31. This was with Marcus Mariota under center. He did a great job in the game, but couldn't do much against the Colts two weeks ago. Last week, the team faced the Giants and the game ended in a tie. I can't believe it is 2026 and games still end in a tie, but here we are. Much worse, the Commanders were in field goal range, and they somehow got sacked. It ran out the clock, and the game ended. Complete mismanagement of the situation. COMMANDERS RUN OUT THE CLOCK ON THEMSELVES, SETTLE FOR TIE WITH GIANTS IN OVERTIME MELTDOWN The San Francisco 49ers have been elite this season with a 5-0 record. They are the Super Bowl favorites, and really look like they might be one of the few minimally flawed teams in football. Last year seemed like one riddled with injuries. They still found a way to get to the playoffs. What we are seeing, though, is a healthier team, back together, and rolling. They started by crushing the Rams in the first game. Then, returning home, they destroyed the Dolphins. Up until last week, the only game that was close was between them and the Cardinals in Week 3. Perhaps Arizona is better than we expected; after all, they beat the Rams yesterday. The Broncos came into town two weeks ago, and the 49ers won by 10. Last week they faced the Seahawks and won on the road by three points. This was a revenge game for San Francisco. What I think has been most impressive about the 49ers is that they have been able to win with the run, the pass, defense, and in a variety of ways. That makes them more versatile than a team like the Bills, who rely on one person to do everything. NFL WEEK 5 SUNDAY TAKEAWAYS: RODGERS DEFIES FATHER TIME, COEN GETS BAILED OUT, 49ERS SURVIVE UGLY PERFORMANCE CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The 49ers have the 11th-best team vs. the opponent's running game in terms of yards allowed. They are seventh against the pass, so the Commanders' offense will have a tough task of stopping them. The Commanders are terrible against the pass, having the fourth-worst defense in football. They are better against the run. Last time the two teams played, George Kittle was a star with two touchdown receptions. Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel could both be out for this game. Kittle is +110 to score a touchdown. I'm going to take a different shot, though. I'll take Purdy to throw for 3+ touchdowns at +130. The Commanders' defense and Purdy's success this season make me think this is a good shot. For more sports betting information and plays, follow David on X/Twitter: @futureprez2024

articles.title: Bo Nix Benching Addressed by Payton Ahead of Broncos vs. Cardinals Amid Ryan Fitzpatrick's Criticism
articles.summary: Denver Broncos coach Sean Payton was unequivocal when discussing the possible demotion of starting quarterback Bo Nix.
articles.body:
Denver Broncos coach Sean Payton was unequivocal when discussing the possible demotion of starting quarterback Bo Nix.

Payton ruled out a QB change ahead of a Week 7 meeting with the Arizona Cardinals.

"He's going to become the byproduct of all the finer things that get improved: the improved play from our offensive line, the more efficient we are relative to balance, running the football, and that's our job as coaches here," the coach said of Nix. "We talked about after the game about how we're excited to get that win but at the same time find all the improvement we need in all areas. So, it starts with all of us."

Nix has received steady criticism throughout the 2026 NFL season. Nobody has come down harder on him than retired quarterback Ryan Fitzpatrick, who laid into him after the 17-14 overtime win over the Seattle Seahawks on the Prime Video broadcast.

Payton sidestepped a question about Fitzpatrick's viral criticism.

"I try to focus on the next day here," he said . "We're trying to focus on getting ready for Arizona."

Nix went 17-of-27 for 107 yards against the Seahawks. He's averaging 174.8 yards per game and has six touchdown passes in as many starts. In general, the third-year signal-caller isn't testing defenses down the field or posing a threat as a runner.

Denver's 14-3 finish and trip to the AFC title game in 2025 raised the expectations for everybody in the building. Especially as he inches toward the end of his rookie contract, Nix needs to take his game to another level, and that isn't happening right now.

The passion behind Fitzpatrick's assessment was striking and the reason it garnered more attention than the usual analysis after a game. Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio floated the idea that Fitzpatrick was effectively speaking for somebody within the Broncos organization:

A lot of the team's fans may felt the same way Fitzpatrick did after watching the Seattle game.

Still, as frustrating as Nix might be, the alternative for Denver isn't any better. Jarrett Stidham is the backup, with Sam Ehlinger third on the depth chart.

Payton is well aware of that along with the kind of optics he'd create by benching the 2024 first-round pick.

articles.title: Buying or Selling Biggest NFL Rumors After Week 6
articles.summary: As we near the midpoint of the 2026 NFL season, rumors are swirling about potential trade moves, a prominent free agent, contract negotiations and a head coach under heavy criticism.
articles.body:
As we near the midpoint of the 2026 NFL season, rumors are swirling about potential trade moves, a prominent free agent, contract negotiations and a head coach under heavy criticism.

Teams often use the bye week to re-evaluate the roster and coaching strategies, which can spur change. The Buffalo Bills, Jacksonville Jaguars, Los Angeles Chargers and Washington Commanders have a Week 7 bye.

There's some buzz around the winless Chargers and Commanders, who mismanaged the clock in a Week 5 game against the New York Giants.

Here's a six-pack of the biggest league rumors following Week 6, with a verdict on whether to buy or sell the report.

Browns Are Open to Re-Signing QB Deshaun Watson

One of this season's biggest surprises, the Cleveland Browns lead the AFC North with a 4-2 record, thanks in part to Deshaun Watson's play.

Cleveland.com's Mary Kay Cabot wrote about the possibility that Cleveland re-signs Watson, who's in the final year of his fully guaranteed contract.

"… If he continues to play well — he's currently No. 8 in the NFL with a 101.2 rating — the Browns will consider re-signing him after the season. The season is still young and a lot can happen, but Watson has demonstrated that he's got plenty left in the tank and is flourishing under Todd Monken .

For context, Watson has thrown for multiple touchdowns in two of six games but for fewer than 165 yards in three of those outings. Compared to previous years, he's playing at a high level, but that's a low bar for him.

The Browns have two 2027 first-round picks: their own and one from the 2-4 Los Angeles Rams. They may prefer drafting a quarterback on a rookie deal over re-signing Watson, who's solid but still less than the three-time Pro Bowl player from his Houston Texans years.

Watson will need to significantly increase his passing production and lead the Browns to a playoff win to earn serious consideration for a new deal in Cleveland, which seems like an improbable task.

Chargers Won't Hold Fire Sale at Trade Deadline

The Los Angeles Chargers are one of three winless teams following Week 6, but according to The Ringer's NFL insider Tom Pelissero , they're not giving up on the season or their players.

"Teams are calling Chargers GM Joe Hortiz, who has told multiple GMs the same thing about any potential trade offers: We're not interested," Pelissero wrote in his Substack, The Sweep.

Pelissero sourced this before the Chargers' Week 6 22-6 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. If Los Angeles had won that game or come close to pulling off an upset, you could argue the Chargers may be on the verge of a turnaround, but that's not the case.

Los Angeles has a Week 7 bye, and Hortiz should have tough discussions about the team's direction and short-term future. The Chargers are headed nowhere with double-digit losses in four out of six games.

Hortiz should take calls on any player on an expiring contract, like edge-rusher Khalil Mack, cornerback Donte Jackson, defensive tackle Dalvin Tomlinson and inside linebacker Daiyan Henley. They need a reset that includes a change at offensive coordinator. The Jim Harbaugh-Mike McDaniel football marriage isn't working out.

Chiefs Reunion with WR Tyreek Hill Isn't Imminent

After the Kansas City Chiefs lost wideout Tyquan Thornton for the season, many expected them to reunite with free agent wide receiver Tyreek Hill.

But that might not happen for a few reasons. The Athletic's Jonathan Jones outlined three factors complicating Hill's situation.

"The health of Hill's knee is one factor," Jones wrote. "The money will be another, as no one expects him to sign a veteran minimum deal. And then there's the potential NFL discipline. Put those in whatever order you'd like, but nothing seems imminent."

A Miami jury found Hill liable for two counts of battery against his estranged wife in a civil trial.

With those factors in mind, Kansas City could develop second-year pro Jalen Royals or rookie fifth-rounder Cyrus Allen while Rashee Rice works his way back to action from a hamstring injury.

By the way, the Chiefs are 5-0, so they don't need help right now.

Jaguars Won't Trade WR Brian Thomas Jr. Until It's Close to the Deadline

After the Arizona Cardinals traded wideout Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Houston Texans, Jacksonville Jaguars receiver Brian Thomas Jr. has been in the trade rumor mill.

Yet The Athletic's Jonathan Jones doesn't believe the Jaguars will budge on any offers for Thomas as of now.

"Jacksonville hasn't been in a rush to deal Thomas, and I suspect that will remain the case until we get closer to the trade deadline," Jones wrote.

Thomas' role in the Jaguars' offense has completely evaporated. He hasn't caught a pass in two weeks and saw only five targets in the team's back-to-back games in London.

Meanwhile, rookie sixth-rounder Josh Cameron's role has grown, and two-way player Travis Hunter caught four passes for 59 yards and a touchdown and played cornerback in the Jaguars' last outing.

In Jacksonville, Thomas is expendable, and teams will give him a chance to rediscover his 2024 Pro Bowl form, when he caught 87 passes for 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns.

The Jaguars have a Week 7 bye; don't be surprised if Thomas is the next trade domino to fall before November.

Vikings Will Be Active Ahead of Trade Deadline

At 5-0, the Minnesota Vikings may not be complacent. Typically, teams pushing for the playoffs are most active, while clubs atop the standings stand pat.

According to The Athletic's Alec Lewis , Vikings general manager Nolan Teasley is open to making moves before the trade deadline.

" Team sources, who requested anonymity so they could share details of the team's plans without facing repercussions from management, suggest he is open to pursuing a bevy of ideas at the trade deadline.

"Player availability, asking price and salary-cap dynamics will determine the extent to which the Vikings supplement their roster before Nov. 10. And even though most NFL teams remain committed to winning, it's worth assessing the areas that could solidify the team's floor and raise its ceiling ."

Minnesota is the least likely unbeaten team because of inconsistent quarterback play. Kyler Murray missed a game while in concussion protocol, and even when healthy, he's posted modest numbers in two of three full starts.

The Vikings could shake up their wide receiver room by adding and/or subtracting players to help Murray improve.

According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , Jauan Jennings could be on the move. Mostly ineffective in the Vikings offense, he has just two catches for nine yards in four games.

Keep in mind that Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison have missed games due to injuries. To add insurance at wide receiver, Minnesota could trade Jennings and acquire another veteran to complement Jefferson and Addison.

HC Dan Quinn Could Be Fired If Commanders Lose in Monday Night Blowout

After the Washington Commanders' head-scratching Week 5 tie with the New York Giants, Dan Quinn is under a microscope.

NFL Network's Mike Garafolo said, "Anything is on the table" if Washington lacks effort or has a lopsided loss to the San Francisco 49ers Monday night.

Quarterback Jayden Daniels took accountability for the late-game clock-management debacle, but ultimately the head coach, who runs the operation, must accept blame as well.

The Commanders could cool the temperature on Quinn's hot seat with a signature win, or they must be competitive in a loss.

With Washington on a Week 7 bye to digest everything from the last two weeks, there's legitimate buzz about Quinn's job security.

Maurice Moton covers the NFL for Bleacher Report. You can follow him on Twitter @MoeMoton.

articles.title: 'Dream Team' Rams Ripped by Rival Coach After Cardinals Loss & Garrett Trade, 'Doesn't Work in' NFL
articles.summary: One opposing NFL coach questioned whether the Los Angeles Rams were perhaps a little too aggressive this offseason in their pursuit of Super Bowl glory.
articles.body:
One opposing NFL coach questioned whether the Los Angeles Rams were perhaps a little too aggressive this offseason in their pursuit of Super Bowl glory.

In particular, the coach believes trading two-time Pro Bowler Jared Verse for reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett was a mistake.

"Verse had juice and carried the flag for that team," they told The Athletic's Mike Sando . "Be careful with the dream teams. That doesn't work in this league."

Los Angeles is sitting at 2-4 on the season with Sunday's 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals.

Having watched the team in person, one member of the Cardinals coaching staff downplayed how bad things are for the Rams.

"Dude, they'll be fine. They have Matthew Stafford," the coach said to The MMQB's Albert Breer .

An anonymous coach echoed the same thing to Sando, citing the losses to the Denver Broncos and Buffalo Bills by seven combined points.

"They played Denver to the wire, Buffalo to the wire — good teams," the coach said. "They are going to the wire in just about every game. You win some, you lose some in the NFL. I think they're gonna be fine."

The second-guessing over the Garrett trade is a little unfair because nobody could predict he'd be injured in Week 1. He had missed two combined games between 2021-25.

Rams general manager Les Snead did, however, know what acquiring the Hall of Fame-bound edge-rusher would do to the team's preseason expectations — and how much added pressure that would bring.

No matter how good he looked in workouts, Aaron Donald was always going to have a lot of rust after being retired for two full seasons as well. That, along with Garrett's injury, can help to explain why L.A. has just eight sacks as a team.

A level of regression with Stafford was bound to happen, too, when his touchdown (46) and interception (eight) rates were some of the best of his career.

With the benefit of hindsight, this wasn't an unbeatable "dream team."

But just as people were premature to write the Rams' name in as the NFC's representative for Super Bowl LXI before the season kicked off, the overreactions to their record might be premature.

articles.title: CJGJ Suspended by NFL for Spitting at Raiders' Brock Bowers on Video, Bills Safety Was Ejected
articles.summary: Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson has been suspended for one game without pay after he was flagged for unsportsmanlike conduct and ejected from Sunday's 33-30 win over the Las Vegas Raiders for spitting in the direction of tight end Brock Bowers.
articles.body:
Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson has been suspended for one game without pay after he was flagged for unsportsmanlike conduct and ejected from Sunday's 33-30 win over the Las Vegas Raiders for spitting in the direction of tight end Brock Bowers.

Gardner-Johnson apologized in a social media post after the game.

"My passion and competitive nature have always been a huge part of who I am, but I also understand that there is a line that should never be crossed," Gardner-Johnson said. "The gesture I made toward my opponent was inappropriate, unnecessary, and not a reflection of the respect I have for him or this game. There is no excuse for my actions, and I take full accountability. No matter how emotional or intense the competition gets, I have to hold myself to a higher standard."

The NFL has set a pretty clear precedent for spitting punishments.

Last season, Jalen Carter was ejected before the start of the Philadelphia Eagles' matchup against the Dallas Cowboys. Because he didn't play in that game, the NFL considered it a one-game suspension and didn't punish him further. Later in the season, Cincinnati Bengals wideout Ja'Marr Chase was suspended a game for spitting at Jalen Ramsey.

There is also the matter of Gardner-Johnson's standing with the Bills. The veteran safety has always been a chippy player, which often verges on the line of unsportsmanlike. Coming into the season, Coming into the 2026 campaign, Tim Graham of The Athletic wrote that CJGJ has been "fined 13 times for $194,924 over his seven NFL seasons."

He has since been fined twice this season alongside his looming suspension.

For now, however, the Bills aren't going to cut him. The team has a Week 7 bye before CJGJ misses Week 8's tilt against the Baltimore Ravens.

But Gardner-Johnson is only under contract for the 2026 season. If Buffalo deems his volatility a liability going forward, his release is certainly possible and wouldn't come as a major surprise.

articles.title: Lamar Jackson Injury Update, Latest on Ravens QB's Status and Return Timeline Ahead of Bengals Game
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson could "potentially" practice this week ahead of a showdown with the Cincinnati Bengals as he continues to try to work his way back from an ankle injury, head coach Jesse Minter said on Monday.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson could "potentially" practice this week ahead of a showdown with the Cincinnati Bengals as he continues to try to work his way back from an ankle injury, head coach Jesse Minter said on Monday.

Jackson has missed Baltimore's last two games, a 30-23 overtime victory over the Atlanta Falcons and a 13-10 loss to the Cleveland Browns.

Baltimore (4-2) is currently in a three-way tie for first place in the AFC North, with Cincinnati (3-2) just a half-game back. In other words, this weekend's game looms large.

Jackson's health was a major storyline for the Ravens early in the season, as he exited the Week 4 contest against the Tennessee Titans.

All eyes were on his status ahead of Baltimore's Week 6 game against the Cleveland Browns, and ESPN's Adam Schefter reported in the lead-up that there was "a realistic chance" he would play against the division rivals. However, he was not able to play in that game.

The only way the Ravens can realistically accomplish all their goals this season is with a healthy Jackson on the field, as he is one of the best quarterbacks in the league with a resume that includes two league MVPs, three First-Team All-Pro nods and four Pro Bowl selections.

His ability to make plays with both his arm and legs is nearly unrivaled and creates matchup nightmares for opposing defenses.

Jackson has completed 70.8 percent of his passes for 967 yards, six touchdowns and one interception to go with 144 yards and a score on the ground as a rusher in four games this season.

Fortunately for the Ravens, they do have a capable backup in Tyler Huntley.

Huntley went 2-0 in starts during the 2025 season and then led the overtime win over the Falcons when Jackson was out. While Baltimore needs its star quarterback to be healthy over the long-term course of the season, Huntley has proven he can help the team tread water if needed. But with Cincinnati, the Buffalo Bills and the Jacksonville Jaguars all looming over the next three weeks, the Ravens will need Jackson healthy as quickly as possible.

articles.title: MN Vikings’ Next Opponent Takes Major Blow in Secondary
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts' secondary looks like it will be shorthanded when they visit the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday.
articles.body:
This weekend, the 5-0 Minnesota Vikings got to sit back and relax atop the NFC North while most of the NFL went back to work for Week 6. And now, they await the Indianapolis Colts, who come to town off a horrendous loss to the 0-5 Tennessee Titans.

If that wasn't bad enough, news broke Monday that the 2-4 Colts will likely be without their top cornerback against Kyler Murray and the blossoming Vikings offense on Sunday at U.S. Bank Stadium.

Sauce Gardner doubtful against Minnesota Vikings

Sauce Gardner left Sunday's game against Tennessee with a calf injury. Ian Rapoport (ESPN) notes below that his status is currently week-to-week. From the sounds of it, though, the former No. 4 overall draft pick is highly unlikely to suit up in Minnesota six days from now.

Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 19, 2026

Gardner, who just turned 25 this summer, is in his second season with the Colts. Across six games , he has four passes defended and 17 tackles. He hasn't intercepted a pass since 2024 and injuries have begun to pile up lately.

There was a time Sauce Gardner was among the best cornerbacks in the NFL. That isn't the case this season ( 60.9 grade per PFF – 52nd of 102 CBs ) but his talent is still undeniable.

Vikings facing beat-up Colts secondary… but that's only the start

Depth cornerback Cameron Mitchell is already on injured reserve, which means the Colts will likely look to Cam Taylor-Britt for reps.

Their secondary also includes former MN Vikings safety Cam Bynum and MN Gophers product Justin Walley. Don't forget about former Vikings QB Daniel Jones returning to U.S. Bank Stadium too…

Meanwhile, Kyler Murray is coming off his best game as a Viking, where he completed 24 of 30 passes for 229 yards and a touchdown Week 5 against the Saints. But really, the Colts have way bigger problems than what's happening on the injury report or even the outcome of their next game.

On Monday morning, owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon fired general manager Chris Ballard , saying the Colts' standard is to compete for championships and a change in leadership was needed to get there.

With Ballard out, more sweeping changes could be coming soon. So far Shane Steichen remains employed as the head coach, but after a 9-win first season, he has gone 8-9 twice and could be on the hot seat.

If Indianapolis is going to make further changes following a loss to the Minnesota Vikings, you can bet teams will be calling interim GM Ed Dodds about running back Jonathan Taylor. The timing that these two organizations are meeting is especially intriguing, given the opposite direction they're traveling.

articles.title: Nick Sirianni expresses trust in medical staff after Jalen Hurts update
articles.summary: Nick Sirianni expressed full confidence in the Eagles’ medical staff when asked about Jalen Hurts playing in London before his updated diagnosis
articles.body:
Nick Sirianni expressed confidence in the Eagles ' medical staff Monday when asked about Jalen Hurts playing in London before additional testing revealed blood clots in both lungs.

Hurts is out for the season, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. The Eagles and his agent, Nicole Lynn, announced that the quarterback has deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli , is clinically stable, and is expected to make a full recovery without long-term effects.

"I'm not a medical expert," Sirianni said. "I lean on our medical experts in every situation. I have full trust and full faith in them."

The questions followed Rapoport's report that Hurts remained in the hospital until 4 a.m. before Philadelphia's game against Jacksonville and played without having slept. The joint statement said specialists in London initially diagnosed superficial left calf vein thrombosis before further testing and monitoring confirmed the current diagnosis.

Sirianni emphasized the organization's concern for its players when discussing Hurts' participation.

"The health of our players is always at the forefront of our minds," Sirianni said. "We'll leave that up to the medical experts. We always care deeply about our players."

Those comments offered no additional details about the evaluations or clearance process before the London game. They reinforced Sirianni's position that specialists overseeing player care make medical decisions.

Hurts is receiving blood thinners and cannot participate in contact activities during treatment. The Eagles and Lynn expect he will be able to resume contact football once he is off the medication, though their statement did not provide a return timetable.

articles.title: Stephen A. Smith reveals somber ‘hope’ for Eagles’ Jalen Hurts after scary blood clot diagnosis
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts will miss the remainder of the 2026 NFL season after doctors diagnosed him with deep vein thrombosis and bilatera...
articles.body:
Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts will miss the remainder of the 2026 NFL season after doctors diagnosed him with deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, according to a joint statement from the Eagles and his agent, Nicole Lynn. The 27-year-old is clinically stable, and his medical team expects him to make a full recovery, but cannot participate in football activities while taking blood thinners.

After the announcement, ESPN's Stephen A. Smith expressed hope that Hurts will be willing to be open with how the diagnosis came about, per a post on X by ClutchPoints.

"I hope that at some point in time, once he discovers how this happened, he's open and forthcoming about it so many other people can be helped," he said.

The diagnosis developed from an issue initially identified in Hurts' left calf before Philadelphia's recent game against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London. An ultrasound performed after the Eagles arrived in London revealed a superficial vein thrombosis. Doctors subsequently identified movement in the clot during a follow-up ultrasound in Philadelphia, and further medical evaluations revealed deep vein thrombosis and blood clots affecting both lungs.

Hurts played against Jacksonville on Sunday, completing 21 of 40 passes for 220 yards and one touchdown in a 19-17 loss. According to NFL Insider Tom Pelissero, he had been awake for approximately 36 consecutive hours before the matchup, per Yahoo Sports. Insider John Clark later reported that doctors had instructed Hurts not to sleep. It is currently unclear when Hurts might be cleared to participate in football again.

Hurts had recorded 933 passing yards, eight touchdown passes and three interceptions through five games in the 2026 season. He has led Philadelphia to two Super Bowl appearances and earned Super Bowl MVP honors when the Eagles defeated the Kansas City Chiefs fin Super Bowl LIX.

articles.title: Rams Kicker Blake Grupe's Updated Injury Timeline After Replacing 'Thiccer Kicker' Harrison Mevis
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams have a kicker problem.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams have a kicker problem.

Blake Grupe—who was signed this week to replace Harrison Mevis—suffered a knee injury during Sunday's matchup against the Arizona Cardinals while covering a kickoff. He was officially placed on injured reserve on Monday, ruling him out for at least four weeks.

Mevis was just 5-for-9 on field goals this season, which included a miss and blocked attempt during last week's 37-34 overtime loss against the Buffalo Bills. His release didn't come as a major surprise.

Special teams have been an issue for the Rams in general—last season, head coach Sean McVay fired special-teams coordinator Chase Blackburn late in the season after gaffes from that unit contributed to a number of losses.

"This isn't the first time that we've had adversity and the first time that we've had some different things that I have to do a better job of," McVay said of his special teams' group this season. "We'll lean in. We'll go back to work. We'll use these as growth opportunities."

Grupe, 27, was expected to upgrade the kicker position. He started his career with the New Orleans Saints (2023-25) before a five-game stint with the Indianapolis Colts last season, where he was 11-for-11 on field goals and 10-for-10 on extra points. For his career he's 86-for-105 on field goals.

"Those five weeks in Indy were seriously big for me, big for my career," he told reporters this past week. "I was able to get the ball rolling and show what I can do, and that was big for me."

But the Colts gave the starting kicker position back to the previously injured Spencer Shrader over the summer and released Grupe, who then picked up with the New York Jets on their practice squad before the Rams signed him this week.

Unfortunately for both Grupe and the Rams, injury very quickly struck. It had an immediate impact on Sunday—after scoring their first touchdown, the team went for a two-point try instead of kicking and failed to convert. And now, the Rams will have to find a new kicker.
